title: Switchcraft: AI Model Router for Agentic Tool Calling
cost_reduction_reported: 82.9% accuracy, matching/exceeding best single model, with 84% lower inference cost (over $3,600 saved per million queries)
summary: Switchcraft is an inline model router for agentic tool calls that picks the cheapest model predicted to produce a correct call, using a DistilBERT classifier under a latency budget. It matches the best model's accuracy at 84% lower cost and finds larger models do not reliably win on tool use.
key_idea: Per-tool-call routing to the cheapest correct model.
relevance_rationale: Tool-call-level routing inside agents.

title: Local-Splitter: A Measurement Study of Seven Tactics for Reducing Cloud LLM Token Usage on Coding-Agent Workloads
cost_reduction_reported: Local routing + prompt compression gives 45-79% cloud token savings on edit- and explanation-heavy coding-agent workloads; full tactic set incl. draft-review gives 51% on RAG-heavy
summary: A measurement study of seven tactics for cutting cloud-LLM tokens when a small local model triages requests in front of a frontier model in coding agents: local routing, compression, semantic caching, local draft with cloud review, minimal diffs, intent extraction and batching with prompt caching. The tactics are delivered via an MCP/OpenAI-compatible shim.
key_idea: Small local model as a triage layer in front of a frontier model for coding agents; the best tactic mix depends on the workload.
relevance_rationale: Practical big-small split for coding agents, with measured token and dollar savings and open-source tooling.

title: Scaling Small Agents Through Strategy Auctions
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces reliance on the largest agent by 53% and overall cost by 35%
summary: Shows small agents lag on complex tasks and proposes SALE, where agents of different sizes bid short strategic plans scored by a cost-value mechanism, enabling per-task routing and self-improvement without a separate router.
key_idea: Auction among differently sized agents for per-task routing.
relevance_rationale: Direct cost reduction via routing among small and large agents.

title: The advisor strategy: Give Sonnet an intelligence boost with Opus
cost_reduction_reported: Sonnet executor + Opus advisor: +2.7 points on SWE-bench Multilingual over Sonnet alone with 11.9% lower cost per agentic task; Haiku + Opus advisor: 41.2% vs 19.7% on BrowseComp, trailing Sonnet solo by 29% but 85% cheaper per task
summary: Anthropic's advisor tool lets a cheaper executor model run an agentic task end to end and consult a stronger advisor model mid-task for a plan or correction, all inside one API request, with advisor tokens billed at advisor rates. Vendor benchmarks show quality gains with lower or similar cost, especially for weaker executors.
key_idea: Cheap executor runs the loop and calls an expensive advisor only at hard decision points.
relevance_rationale: Productized step-level escalation pattern with vendor-reported cost and quality numbers.

title: Optimizing for cost and intelligence
cost_reduction_reported: Examples reported: prompt caching cut DeepResearch Bench II cost 81% (Fable 5.1) and 62.5% (Sonnet 5); on SWE-bench Pro, Opus 5.5 low effort with failures re-run at high reached 97% at ~$0.17/task vs 95.3% at $0.29 all-high; Fable 5 coordinator + Sonnet 5 worker cost ~50% of solo Fable 5 on an easy BrowseComp slice; on full BrowseComp, solo Fable 5 at lower effort was 22-30% cheaper than the orchestrator at same accuracy
summary: Anthropic documentation with measured results on cost levers: caching, trimming tools and context, effort tuning, retrying failures at higher effort, task budgets, advisor pairing and orchestrator-worker delegation. It reports that advisor gains shrink as the executor approaches the advisor's capability and that cheaper-worker delegation helps on easy slices but can lose to a solo model at lower effort on the full set.
key_idea: Vendor-measured playbook of per-step and architecture cost levers, including when delegation to cheaper workers loses.
relevance_rationale: Rare quantitative vendor evidence comparing escalation, effort control and orchestrator-worker model splits on agentic benchmarks.

title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
cost_reduction_reported: Agentic coding uses ~1000x more tokens than code chat; runs on the same task vary up to 30x; Kimi-K2 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 use over 1.5M more tokens than GPT-5 on average
summary: The first systematic token-consumption study of coding agents across eight frontier models on SWE-bench Verified. Input tokens dominate cost, usage is highly stochastic, accuracy saturates at intermediate cost, human difficulty ratings poorly predict tokens, and models underestimate their own token use.
key_idea: Where coding-agent tokens go and why they are hard to predict.
relevance_rationale: Seed-type token-consumption analysis of coding agents.

cost_reduction_reported: 75.54% accuracy at USD 1.00 per 1,000 queries; ranked second on RouterArena (arena score 72.08)
summary: OrcaRouter fits per-arm ridge regressors offline from a full-information reward matrix on curated prompts, then deploys as a LinUCB contextual bandit that can keep learning from bandit feedback.
key_idea: Offline warm-start plus online LinUCB updates for a production-oriented router.
relevance_rationale: Practical hybrid offline-online router design with public leaderboard results.

summary: ServiceNow researchers argue a coding agent with only a terminal and filesystem, calling platform APIs directly, solves many enterprise automation tasks better and far more cheaply than MCP tool agents or GUI web agents. Suggests simple programmatic interfaces plus strong models as the enterprise backbone.

summary: A 7B searcher first scouts the repository and produces a sandbox-verified handoff, and a router uses its hidden states to dispatch the issue to one of four frontier fixers. Cost per solve drops to about a fifth, and an ablation shows the cheap-model handoff itself, lifting cheaper fixers, drives the gain.

The team is not significantly better, its value comes entirely from the executor, and with equal cost multi-agent structure adds cost without clear benefit.

cost_reduction_reported: Narrows the gap to the strongest agent while using it for fewer than 25% of calls

It approaches the strongest agent's quality while calling it under 25% of the time.
key_idea: Iterative critique-then-route controller with utilization constraints.

cost_reduction_reported: Per-episode thinking compute reduced 43%-65% vs deferral-only baselines on HotpotQA, MBPP and household-robot tasks, with certified reward and cloud-call-rate guarantees

A convergence probe stops on-device reasoning once the intended action stabilizes, and a perplexity rule defers uncertain actions to a cloud model; both thresholds are jointly calibrated on episode trajectories with Learn-Then-Test for finite-sample guarantees on reward and cloud-call rate.
key_idea: Per-action deferral from a small local model to a cloud model inside ReAct loops, with statistical guarantees.
relevance_rationale: Per-step small-to-large deferral inside a ReAct loop with certified cost control.

cost_reduction_reported: Up to 9.3% higher accuracy while reducing GPU cost from 186.26 GiB to 1.04 GiB
summary: GraphPlanner generates routing workflows per query as an MDP, choosing at each step both an LLM backbone and an agent role (planner, executor, summarizer), with graph memory of past interactions and RL optimizing accuracy and efficiency. It beats single- and multi-round routers and generalizes to unseen tasks and models.

title: Introducing FireRouter with Opus
cost_reduction_reported: Internal A/B test (>1 month, sessions randomised to router vs Opus-only): cost per session $15.36 -> $6.63 (57% +/- 19 ppts lower); graded-turn accuracy 78.7% vs 80.2% (98.1% of Opus-only); cache hit rate 94.2% vs 97.8% (vendor-reported)
summary: Fireworks releases a per-turn, cache-aware router for coding agents that routes each user turn among Claude Opus 5.5, GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash, trading off estimated suitability against cost including the prompt-cache value lost by switching. It reports a randomised A/B test on internal coding traffic, scoring accuracy by task completion, correctness and whether the user corrected the next turn.
key_idea: Turn-level routing in coding agents with explicit pricing of cache loss, validated by a randomised live-traffic A/B test.
relevance_rationale: Step-level cost-aware routing in a production agent with a controlled live-traffic experiment (vendor-run).

title: The frontier isn't a model. It's a router.
cost_reduction_reported: DeepSWE v1.1 oracle over 18 models: 97.6% pass@1 at $1.88/task vs best single model GPT-6 Astra 74.1% at $6.52; open-models-only oracle 90.3% at $1.45; best pair +13.1 pts, best trio 91.2%. Production: FireRouter sessions $7.42 vs $15.81 for Opus 5 alone (53% reduction, 2,334 sessions over four weeks of internal coding traffic) (vendor-reported)
summary: Runs 18 models on every DeepSWE task to measure the per-task oracle routing ceiling, showing most of the gain comes from two or three complementary models and most oracle picks are cheap models. It stresses that oracle upside is upward-biased and that real routers fail on model recall (citing LLMRouterBench), then reports four weeks of internal production coding traffic through task-level, cache-aware FireRouter.
key_idea: Complementary models give a large oracle headroom for task-level routing in coding agents, but capturing it requires predicting the winner before execution.
relevance_rationale: Agentic-task routing ceiling analysis plus production cost numbers.

title: Free the models: Harness design at the frontier
cost_reduction_reported: DeepSWE v1.1: Replit Agent 72% at $2.11/task vs GPT-6 Astra (mini-swe-agent) 67% at $1.60 (low effort) and 74% at $4.43 (xhigh); sidekick architecture 61% at $1.34. Terminal-Bench 4.0: 49% at $2.53 vs Astra 42% at $2.25 (low) and 60% at $5.86 (xhigh); sidekick 33% at $1.84 (means of 4 runs; vendor-reported). Production delegation rates: 21-36% of turns dispatch a subagent
summary: Replit argues that an external router is always less capable than the model it routes for, and instead lets the main agent choose at each step its own effort (changed mid-turn without cache loss on GPT-6), whether to delegate, and which subagent tier (small/standard/large), effort and specialist to use, including reusing already-briefed subagents. It reports production delegation statistics per model and a Pareto comparison against single-model baselines and a one-worker sidekick design.
key_idea: Let the frontier orchestrator itself assign tiers and effort to subagents rather than routing externally.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses step/subagent-level downscaling in production agents with cost-quality results; useful counter-position to external routers.

title: Steer, Don't Solve: Training Small Critic Models for Large Code Agents
cost_reduction_reported: 30-92x lower critic cost than a strong teacher; on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B both more accurate (25.2% vs 20.8%) and cheaper ($0.04 vs $0.11)
summary: Freezes the code agent and trains a small critic on agent trajectories to steer strategy-level reasoning; the critic transfers to unseen agents and improves accuracy at lower cost.
key_idea: A small trained critic steers a large agent cheaply.
relevance_rationale: Cheap signal plus specialization improving cost-quality.

title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Full-trajectory escalation recovers less than half of the cheap-to-strong quality gap at a substantial cost premium; downshifting offers a favorable cost-quality point
models_studied: Claude and GPT low- and high-capability model pairs
summary: Studies mid-trajectory model handoffs in coding agents, varying direction, timing and how much of the prior trajectory the receiving model sees. Escalating a cheap model's trajectory to a strong one recovers under half the gap at high cost (the handoff tax), while downshifting after hard reasoning is favorable; less inherited context helps escalation.
key_idea: Mid-trajectory model switches carry a handoff tax; downshifting works better than escalating.
relevance_rationale: Key empirical evidence for in-trajectory model switching.

title: AgentCollab: A Self-Evaluation-Driven Collaboration Paradigm for Efficient LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier (no single number in abstract)
summary: AgentCollab runs a cheap model by default and escalates control to a stronger model only when the agent's own self-reflection indicates it is not making progress, with a difficulty-aware cumulative escalation that allocates more budget after recent failures. The search summary notes that putting the large model on execution rather than planning gave higher accuracy.
key_idea: Self-evaluated progress triggers escalation to a stronger model mid-trajectory.
relevance_rationale: Step-level escalation without an external router.

title: The Replay Gap: Static Evaluation of Model Switching in LLM Agents Scores the Wrong World
summary: Tests the common practice of evaluating in-agent model switching by replaying logged trajectories, using live forked SWE-bench rollouts. Swaps rewrite 61-94% of subsequent actions and replay evaluation mispredicts every success-relevant outcome, so static replay scores the wrong world.
key_idea: Offline replay badly misestimates the effect of mid-trajectory model swaps.
relevance_rationale: Crucial caveat for learning step-level routing from logs.

title: Atlas: Optimizing Deployment of Compound AI Workflows on Heterogeneous Clusters
cost_reduction_reported: Selects plans within 0.03 of oracle accuracy while reducing deployment cost by up to 42% via heterogeneous placement; up to 2.6x lower profiling cost
summary: Atlas picks models per workflow stage and places them on a heterogeneous cluster via MILP, using a Markovian accuracy predictor that composes stage-to-stage accuracy transitions instead of full end-to-end profiling.
key_idea: Stage-wise model choice and placement via MILP with composed accuracy estimates.
relevance_rationale: Per-stage model selection with cost/SLOs.

title: RouteNLP: Closed-Loop LLM Routing with Conformal Cascading and Distillation Co-Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: 8-week enterprise pilot (~5K queries/day): 58% lower inference cost at 91% response acceptance, p99 latency 1,847 ms to 387 ms; 40-85% cost reduction retaining 96-100% quality on a six-task benchmark
summary: Closed-loop framework combining a difficulty-aware router, conformal cascading and a loop that clusters escalation failures, distils cheaper models on them and retrains the router. Reports an 8-week enterprise customer-service pilot.
key_idea: Route, cascade, and distil on escalation failures in a closed loop.
relevance_rationale: Production evidence and a closed-loop design that learns from traffic; directly on-premise for enterprise systems.

title: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration

summary: ZEBRA splits a fixed monetary budget across phases of a multi-agent pipeline by having an LLM estimate per-phase utility curves and solving a continuous knapsack with water-filling. It beats letting an LLM allocate directly and adapts splits to pipeline structure.
key_idea: Knapsack-based budget split across pipeline phases.
relevance_rationale: Per-phase budget allocation in MAS.

title: R2V Agent: Teaching SLMs When to Ask for Help

summary: R2V-Agent distills an SLM policy from a teacher LLM (behavior cloning then verifier-guided DPO), then trains a calibrated step-level router on the SLM's residual failures with a CVaR-constrained objective. The router escalates to the LLM only when failure risk warrants, improving the reliability-cost frontier.
key_idea: Calibrated per-step risk router decides when a distilled SLM should hand off to an LLM.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses step-level escalation with distillation.

title: Learning How Much to Collaborate: Difficulty-Aware Topology Selection for Multi-Agent Code Generation

summary: Shows the benefit of hierarchical multi-agent collaboration over a single agent grows strongly with problem difficulty while costing ~10x tokens, and trains a selector that picks the topology maximizing predicted success minus cost. Under budget-matched evaluation it beats always-hierarchical at 40% of its cost.
key_idea: Choose single agent vs MAS topology per problem by predicted difficulty and cost.
relevance_rationale: Direct per-query decision of when MAS is worth it.

title: AgentOpt v0.1 Technical Report: Client-Side Optimization for LLM-Based Agent

summary: AgentOpt is a framework-agnostic client-side package that searches for the most cost-effective assignment of models to pipeline roles from a small evaluation set, using bandit and BO search algorithms. It shows huge cost spreads across model combinations and finds near-optimal assignments cheaply.

summary: For multi-turn agents, Continuum pins the KV cache of requests that issue tool calls with a time-to-live chosen from reload cost and eviction-induced queueing, and combines this with program-level FCFS to keep multi-turn continuity.
key_idea: KV cache TTL across tool calls plus program-level FCFS.
relevance_rationale: Agent-specific KV retention with large JCT gains on real agent workloads.

title: Rethinking Predictive Modeling for LLM Routing: When Simple kNN Beats Complex Learned Routers
summary: Shows that a well-tuned k-nearest-neighbors router matches or beats complex learned routers across instruction-following, QA and reasoning benchmarks, explained by locality of model performance in embedding space. Introduces standardized routing benchmarks including a multimodal one.
key_idea: Simple kNN is a strong router baseline.
relevance_rationale: Practical guidance: start with kNN.
found_via: snowball: cited-by ong-2024-routellm | snowball: cited-by nguyen-2024-metallm

title: Near-Optimal Online Deployment and Routing for Streaming LLMs
summary: StageRoute jointly decides which LLMs to deploy at maintenance windows and how to route each query among live models under budget and throughput constraints, with a near-optimal T^(2/3) regret.
key_idea: Hierarchical bandit for model deployment plus per-query routing.
relevance_rationale: Captures streaming model inventory churn in production.

title: Plan and Budget: Effective and Efficient Test-Time Scaling on Reasoning Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 70% accuracy gains, 39% token reduction and 193.8% improvement in E3; DS-Qwen-32B matches DS-LLaMA-70B efficiency
summary: Models reasoning as a sequence of sub-questions with different uncertainty and allocates token budgets to each sub-question by estimated complexity. Model-agnostic and test-time only.
key_idea: Decompose, then budget tokens per sub-question.
relevance_rationale: Sub-task level budget allocation transferable to agent steps.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking)

title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
cost_reduction_reported: ~5x less test-time compute for the same accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME; 2.5x lower average cost per query when amortised over related queries
summary: Lets models think offline about a context before queries arrive, pre-computing useful inferences so test-time reasoning is cheaper; gains depend on how predictable queries are. Includes an agentic SWE case study.
key_idea: Move reasoning compute to idle time over shared context.
relevance_rationale: Amortising reasoning across agent queries on shared context.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking)

title: Stop Wasting Your Tokens: Towards Efficient Runtime Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces Smolagents token consumption by 29.68% on GAIA without lowering success rate
summary: SupervisorAgent is a lightweight runtime supervisor triggered by an LLM-free filter that intervenes at critical points to correct errors, curb inefficient behavior and clean observations, without changing the base agent. It cuts token usage by about 30% on GAIA at equal success.
key_idea: Runtime supervision triggered cheaply to stop wasteful agent behavior.
relevance_rationale: Architecture-level MAS token reduction.

title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
cost_reduction_reported: simple observation masking roughly halves cost relative to the raw agent while matching (sometimes slightly exceeding) the solve rate of LLM summarization on SWE-bench Verified
summary: Systematic comparison in SWE-agent (with evidence for OpenHands) of LLM-based trajectory summarization versus simply masking older environment observations. Masking is as effective and cheaper; summarization can even lengthen trajectories.
key_idea: Just mask old observations; LLM summarization rarely pays for itself.
relevance_rationale: Strong, cheap baseline for cutting agent context cost with evidence across models.
found_via: The Complexity Trap observation masking LLM summarization agent context

title: Structured Agent Distillation for Large Language Model
cost_reduction_reported: Significant compression with minimal performance drop
summary: Segments ReAct trajectories into reasoning and action spans and applies span-specific distillation losses to align student and teacher, outperforming token-level and imitation baselines.
key_idea: Span-aware distillation of ReAct agents.
relevance_rationale: Distillation method tailored to agent traces.

title: AdaCoT: Pareto-Optimal Adaptive Chain-of-Thought Triggering via Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: On a production traffic test set, reduced CoT triggering rate to as low as 3.18% and average response tokens by 69.06% while maintaining performance on complex tasks
summary: Frames when to invoke CoT as Pareto optimisation and trains the trigger with PPO, adjusting penalties to move along the frontier; selective loss masking stops decision-boundary collapse.
key_idea: RL-tuned CoT triggering evaluated on production traffic.
relevance_rationale: Production-traffic evidence for adaptive reasoning.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking)

title: Prolonged Reasoning Is Not All You Need: Certainty-Based Adaptive Routing for Efficient LLM/MLLM Reasoning
summary: Generates a short answer first and triggers long reasoning only if its perplexity signals low confidence, beating both always-short and always-long reasoning.
key_idea: Cascade from short answer to long reasoning on perplexity.
relevance_rationale: Cascade logic applied to reasoning length.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking)

title: RouterArena: An Open Platform for Comprehensive Comparison of LLM Routers
summary: RouterArena is an open platform and leaderboard for comparing LLM routers, with a dataset covering broad knowledge domains at graded difficulty, multiple metrics and automated leaderboard updates.
key_idea: Open router leaderboard.
relevance_rationale: Router comparison including commercial routers.
found_via: snowball: cited-by ong-2024-routellm | web search: RouterEval benchmark routing LLMs

title: Autellix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs
cost_reduction_reported: program throughput improved 4-15x at the same latency vs vLLM across diverse LLMs and agentic workloads
summary: Treats agent programs, not individual calls, as the scheduling unit: it intercepts LLM calls, attaches program-level context, and uses preemptive scheduling based on each program's completed service to reduce head-of-line blocking for single-threaded and distributed programs.
key_idea: Program-level (least-attained-service style) scheduling of LLM calls.
relevance_rationale: Core agent-aware scheduling work.

title: Beyond Accuracy: A Multi-Dimensional Framework for Evaluating Enterprise Agentic AI Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Accuracy-only optimization yields agents 4.4-10.8x more expensive than cost-aware alternatives with comparable performance (300 enterprise tasks); up to 50x cost variation for similar precision
summary: Proposes CLEAR, an enterprise agent evaluation framework across cost, latency, efficacy, assurance and reliability, arguing accuracy-only benchmarks mislead. Expert evaluation suggests CLEAR predicts production success better than accuracy alone.
key_idea: Multi-dimensional, cost-controlled evaluation for enterprise agents.
relevance_rationale: Supports cost-aware objectives for agent configuration selection.
found_via: search: multi-objective agentic workflow optimization cost accuracy Pareto arXiv | web search: enterprise agent benchmark cost efficiency CLEAR

title: OmniRouter: Budget and Performance Controllable Multi-LLM Routing
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 6.30% accuracy improvement while reducing computational costs by at least 10.15% vs router baselines (abstract)
summary: OmniRouter treats routing as a global constrained optimization that minimizes total cost subject to a performance level, rather than per-query greedy choices. A retrieval-augmented predictor estimates capabilities and costs, and Lagrangian dual decomposition finds allocations under capacity constraints.
key_idea: Batch-level constrained optimization for budget-controllable routing.
relevance_rationale: Explicit global budget control.

title: Model router for Microsoft Foundry (concepts)
summary: A trained language model deployed as a single Foundry endpoint that routes each prompt across OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek and Meta models. Balanced mode picks the cheapest model within about 1-2% of the best predicted quality, Cost mode within about 5-6%, and Quality mode ignores cost; supports model subsets, failover, agent tool use and session affinity for cache reuse. No quantitative savings figures on this page.
key_idea: Managed multi-vendor router with quality-band routing modes.
relevance_rationale: Seed; enterprise router product with explicit cost-quality band semantics.
found_via: seed: Azure AI Foundry model router

title: ReProbe: Efficient Test-Time Scaling of Multi-Step Reasoning by Probing Internal States of Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Match or surpass PRMs up to 810x larger
summary: Trains tiny uncertainty heads on frozen LLM states to verify reasoning steps, with labels from a larger LLM or self-supervision; they rival PRMs up to 810x larger.
key_idea: Tiny heads replace large PRMs for step verification.
relevance_rationale: Near-free step-level signal.
found_via: hf-papers search: uncertainty quantification LLM agents

title: Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors
summary: W4S trains a small (7B) meta-agent with RL for agentic workflow optimization to design workflows that call a stronger executor LLM, outperforming the strongest baseline by 2.9%-24.6% across eleven benchmarks after one GPU hour of training.
key_idea: Weak meta-agent trained with RL designs workflows for strong executors.
relevance_rationale: Cheap optimizer model for workflow design, lowering optimization cost.
found_via: search: Weak-for-Strong meta-agent workflow optimization W4S arXiv

title: Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor
summary: A 7B Conductor trained with RL learns coordination strategies over pools of powerful worker LLMs, designing communication topologies and writing focused instructions, and beats any individual worker on hard reasoning benchmarks. Trained on randomized pools, it adapts to arbitrary agent sets.
key_idea: Small RL-trained conductor orchestrates large worker LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Small-orchestrator/large-worker pattern.

title: A practical guide to building agents
summary: OpenAI's guide, distilled from customer deployments, recommends maximizing a single agent before splitting into manager or decentralized multi-agent patterns. On model selection it advises prototyping with the most capable model for every task to set a baseline, then swapping in smaller models where they remain acceptable, since simple retrieval or intent classification steps may not need the smartest model.
key_idea: Baseline with the strongest model everywhere, then downscale per task; prefer a single agent until complexity demands more.
relevance_rationale: Seed; canonical practitioner recipe for per-step model downscaling and architecture choice.

title: ART (Agent Reinforcement Trainer) and ART-E email agent
cost_reduction_reported: README states a Qwen 2.5 14B email research agent (ART-E) trained with ART outperforms OpenAI o3 at email retrieval; serverless training claims 40% lower cost
summary: Open-source framework for RL fine-tuning of multi-step agents on custom tasks, using RULER (LLM-judge relative scoring) so no hand-labeled rewards are needed. The README links the ART-E case study (blog: openpipe.ai/blog/art-e-mail-agent) where a 14B Qwen email agent beats o3.
key_idea: RL-train small task agents with judge-based rewards to replace frontier models.
relevance_rationale: Practitioner tooling and case study for replacing frontier agents with small RL-tuned ones.
found_via: GitHub README (OpenPipe/ART) fetched; blog page not renderable

title: PredictaBoard: Benchmarking LLM Score Predictability
summary: PredictaBoard benchmarks assessors that predict whether an LLM will fail on a given prompt, scoring LLM-assessor pairs by rejection rate at different error tolerances.
key_idea: Benchmark for instance-level LLM success prediction.
relevance_rationale: Instance-level performance predictors are the core of predictive routers.

title: Learning When to Plan: Efficiently Allocating Test-Time Compute for LLM Agents
summary: Shows always planning before each action (ReAct-style) is costly and can hurt long-horizon performance; trains agents via SFT then RL to decide when to plan.
key_idea: Agents learn when to spend compute on planning.
relevance_rationale: Step-level test-time compute allocation in agents.
found_via: arXiv title search: test-time compute allocation

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: up to 1.83x speedup for single workflows with large prompts and up to 2.19x with many concurrent workflows vs SGLang with hierarchical radix cache
summary: Workflow-aware KV management for multi-agent systems: it models the execution schedule as an Agent Step Graph, evicts prefix-cache nodes of agents far from their next activation, and prefetches KV from CPU for agents scheduled next.
key_idea: Evict and prefetch KV by each agent's distance to its next turn.
relevance_rationale: Multi-agent prefix caching is a direct serving cost lever.

title: Route to Reason: Adaptive Routing for LLM and Reasoning Strategy Selection
cost_reduction_reported: Higher accuracy than the best single model while reducing token usage by over 60% (seven open models, four reasoning strategies)
summary: Route-To-Reason jointly selects the LLM and the reasoning strategy (e.g. CoT variants) for each query under a user budget, using learned embeddings of model-strategy pairs and a routing table of predicted cost and performance.
key_idea: Joint model plus reasoning-strategy routing.
relevance_rationale: Extends routing to configuration choices.
found_via: snowball: cited-by ong-2024-routellm | web search: route between reasoning and non-reasoning models

title: Online Multi-LLM Selection via Contextual Bandits under Unstructured Context Evolution
summary: Studies sequential LLM selection across multi-step query refinement, where the prompt changes in response to earlier outputs. A LinUCB-based algorithm with myopic regret guarantees, plus budget-aware and position-aware variants, needs no offline data.
key_idea: LinUCB for multi-turn LLM selection under evolving context.
relevance_rationale: Online routing over multi-turn interactions; relevant to multi-step settings.

title: APIGen-MT: Agentic Pipeline for Multi-Turn Data Generation via Simulated Agent-Human Interplay
cost_reduction_reported: xLAM-2-fc-r models outperform GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 on tau-bench and BFCL; smaller models surpass larger ones in multi-turn
summary: Generates verified multi-turn agent data via blueprint validation and simulated human-agent interplay, training xLAM-2 models that beat frontier models on tau-bench.
key_idea: Verified multi-turn synthetic data for customer-service style agents.
relevance_rationale: Close to enterprise tool-agent settings.
found_via: hf-papers search: synthetic agent data generation

title: AgentDistill: Training-Free Agent Distillation with Generalizable MCP Boxes
cost_reduction_reported: Small-LM student agents reach performance comparable to OctoTools (GPT-4o) on biomedical and math benchmarks
summary: Training-free agent distillation by reusing Model-Context-Protocol modules generated by teacher agents, letting small-model students approach teacher-level performance.
key_idea: Distill via reusable tool modules, no training.
relevance_rationale: Cheap route to downscale agents.
found_via: hf-papers search: agent distillation small models

title: Transcending Cost-Quality Tradeoff in Agent Serving via Session-Awareness
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable response quality to GPT-4o at 16.5% of the cost; 1.8x quality improvement relative to the tradeoff curve
summary: AgServe is an agent-serving system with a session-aware server that improves KV-cache reuse, a client that cascades models within a session from real-time quality assessment, and a dynamic GPU scheduler. Agents can pick and upgrade models during a session, reaching GPT-4o-level quality at a fraction of the cost on real testbeds.
key_idea: Session-aware per-round model cascading plus KV-cache management for agent serving.
relevance_rationale: Per-round model selection inside agent sessions with large reported savings; systems-level evidence.

title: Sherlock: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Workflow Execution
cost_reduction_reported: 18.3% average accuracy gain vs non-verifying baseline; workflow execution time reduced up to 48.7% vs non-speculative execution; verification cost 26.0% lower than Monte Carlo search-based verification
summary: Selectively verifies error-prone steps of agentic workflows, continues speculatively while verification runs, and rolls back to the last verified output on failure.
key_idea: Speculate past verification and roll back on failure.
relevance_rationale: Balances verification cost and latency in agent workflows.

title: vCache: Verified Semantic Prompt Caching
cost_reduction_reported: up to 12.5x higher cache hit rate and 26x lower error rate than static-threshold and fine-tuned-embedding baselines while meeting the user-specified error bound
summary: Replaces the single global similarity threshold of semantic caches with per-cached-prompt thresholds learned online, and makes a probabilistic hit/explore decision that provably keeps the error rate under a user-chosen bound. This turns semantic caching into a controllable cost-quality tradeoff.
key_idea: Learn per-entry thresholds online to give a guaranteed maximum error rate for semantic cache hits.
relevance_rationale: Principled correctness control for caching; online-learning design mirrors routing under an error budget.
found_via: vCache verified semantic prompt caching error rate guarantee

title: Small Language Models for Agentic Systems: A Survey of Architectures, Capabilities, and Deployment Trade offs
cost_reduction_reported: Claims SLMs with guided decoding can match or surpass LLMs on tool use, function calling and RAG at 10x-100x lower token cost (abstract, synthesized from literature)
summary: Survey arguing small language models suffice for many schema-constrained agentic workloads and formalizing SLM-default, LLM-fallback designs with uncertainty-aware routing and verifier cascades. Proposes metrics such as cost per successful task.
key_idea: SLM-default, LLM-fallback agent design.
relevance_rationale: Directly about downscaling agent calls.
found_via: search: survey LLM routing | OpenAlex search: LLM agent cascade small large | hf-papers search: small language model function calling

title: Hawkeye:Efficient Reasoning with Model Collaboration
signals_used: concise CoT instructions from large model
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable quality using only 35% of full CoTs; up to 3.4x faster end-to-end reasoning and up to 60% lower inference cost on complex math
summary: A large model writes a short, information-dense CoT (trained by RL to remove redundancy) and a small model expands it into the final response.
key_idea: Large model thinks briefly, small model writes.
relevance_rationale: Large/small split of reasoning vs generation.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking)

title: SATER: A Self-Aware and Token-Efficient Approach to Routing and Cascading
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable performance while reducing computational costs by over 50% and cascade latency by over 80% (abstract)
summary: SATER fine-tunes small models with shortest-response preference optimization and a confidence-aware rejection mechanism so they work in both pre-generation routing and cascade modes. It cuts redundant output and latency.
key_idea: Train the SLM to know when to refuse and escalate.
relevance_rationale: Dual routing/cascade efficiency.

title: Cost-Aware Contrastive Routing for LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: Improves accuracy-cost tradeoff by up to 25% (abstract)
summary: CSCR maps prompts and models into a shared embedding space, using logit footprints for open models and perplexity fingerprints for API models, and trains a contrastive encoder to favor the cheapest accurate model within cost bands. Routing reduces to one kNN lookup with microsecond latency and no retraining when the pool changes.
key_idea: Cost-spectrum contrastive embeddings with kNN routing.
relevance_rationale: Fast, pool-agnostic router.

title: Building State-of-the-Art Enterprise Agents 90x Cheaper with Automated Prompt Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: GEPA-optimized gpt-oss-120b surpasses Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Opus 4.1 baselines by ~3% while being ~22x and ~90x cheaper to serve on IE Bench; GEPA ~20% cheaper to serve than SFT alternatives
summary: Databricks reports that automated prompt optimization (GEPA and others in Agent Bricks) lets an open model beat frontier proprietary models on an enterprise information-extraction benchmark at a fraction of the serving cost, and compares favorably with supervised fine-tuning on lifetime cost.
key_idea: Optimize prompts for a cheap open model instead of paying for a frontier model.
relevance_rationale: Practitioner evidence that config/prompt optimization plus model downscaling yields large cost savings on enterprise-style tasks; not real traffic.
found_via: search: Databricks GEPA prompt optimization enterprise agents cheaper models blog

title: Semantic Agreement Enables Efficient Open-Ended LLM Cascades
cost_reduction_reported: Semantic cascades match or surpass target-model quality at 40% of the cost and reduce latency by up to 60%
summary: For open-ended generation, uses meaning-level agreement among several cheap models' outputs as the deferral signal instead of token confidence. Works with black-box APIs and is robust to model updates.
key_idea: Semantic consensus of cheap ensemble outputs as a black-box deferral signal.
relevance_rationale: Training-free, API-compatible deferral for open-ended outputs.

title: IRT-Router: Effective and Interpretable Multi-LLM Routing via Item Response Theory
summary: IRT-Router borrows item response theory to jointly model LLM abilities and query difficulty/attributes, giving both accurate performance prediction and interpretable parameters. An online warm-up based on semantic similarity helps cold-start queries; experiments span 20 LLMs and 12 datasets.
key_idea: Psychometric IRT model of model ability vs query difficulty for routing.
relevance_rationale: Seed; interpretable difficulty estimation useful for enterprise auditing.

title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding
cost_reduction_reported: matches or outperforms ReAct baselines on Deep Research and SWE tasks with a 10x smaller active context, and beats summarization-based context management
summary: Agents learn to branch into a sub-trajectory for a subtask and fold it on return, keeping only a short summary of the outcome in the main context. An RL method (FoldGRPO) with process rewards trains effective decomposition and context management.
key_idea: Learned branch-and-fold keeps agent working context small.
relevance_rationale: Learned context management for long-horizon agents; subagent-like decomposition inside one model.
found_via: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding

title: Arch-Router: Aligning LLM Routing with Human Preferences
summary: Arch-Router is a 1.5B model that maps queries to user-defined domain or action preferences, which are then bound to specific models. New models can be added by editing the policy mapping without retraining; the authors report state-of-the-art preference matching against proprietary models.
key_idea: Route by matching queries to human-written policy descriptions rather than benchmark scores.
relevance_rationale: Seed; practical preference-aligned router from the Arch gateway team.
found_via: seed | OpenAlex title search | seed list: LLM gateway (katanemo archgw)

title: C3PO: Optimized Large Language Model Cascades with Probabilistic Cost Constraints for Reasoning
cost_reduction_reported: State-of-the-art accuracy and cost-efficiency vs cascading baselines (no single number in abstract)
summary: Self-supervised cascade optimisation that minimises regret against the most powerful model using only unlabelled outputs. Conformal prediction bounds the probability that inference cost exceeds a user budget, with generalisation guarantees.
key_idea: Label-free cascade tuning with conformal cost-overrun control.
relevance_rationale: Label-free, budget-controlled cascades for reasoning.

title: Doing More with Less: A Survey on Routing Strategies for Resource Optimisation in Large Language Model-Based Systems
summary: Survey of routing strategies in LLM-based systems covering when, why and how to route queries to smaller or specialized components to save cost and energy.
key_idea: Survey of routing for resource optimization.
relevance_rationale: Core routing survey.

title: ICL-Router: In-Context Learned Model Representations for LLM Routing
summary: ICL-Router represents each candidate model through in-context vectors built from its performance on a profiling query set, and trains an LLM-based router to predict whether a model will answer a new query correctly. New models can be integrated without retraining.
key_idea: In-context model capability vectors for retrain-free router extension.
relevance_rationale: Addresses model-pool churn.

title: ScoreFlow: Mastering LLM Agent Workflows via Score-based Preference Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: 8.2% improvement over baselines on six benchmarks; enables smaller models to outperform larger ones with lower inference costs
summary: ScoreFlow trains a workflow generator with Score-DPO, a DPO variant that uses quantitative feedback, performing gradient-based optimization in a continuous space rather than discrete search. It improves over prior workflow optimizers across QA, coding and math.
key_idea: Preference-optimize a workflow generator using score-aware DPO.
relevance_rationale: Automated workflow optimization with a smaller-model-beats-larger cost angle.

title: Optimal-Agent-Selection: State-Aware Routing Framework for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 23.8% improvement over baselines; data collection overhead reduced up to 90.1% vs exhaustive search
summary: STRMAC routes each step of multi-agent collaboration to the single most suitable agent using separate encodings of interaction history and agent knowledge, with self-evolving data generation to cheaply collect training paths.
key_idea: Per-step single-agent selection in MAS.
relevance_rationale: Step-level routing among agents.
found_via: snowball: cited-by S2 citations of relevance-5 records

title: When to Reason: Semantic Router for vLLM
cost_reduction_reported: +10.2 pp accuracy on MMLU-Pro while reducing latency 47.1% and tokens 48.5% vs direct inference with vLLM (abstract)
summary: A semantic router classifies whether a query needs reasoning mode and enables chain-of-thought only when beneficial, integrated with vLLM.
key_idea: Route reasoning on/off per query.
relevance_rationale: Cheap reasoning-mode control.
found_via: snowball: cited-by ong-2024-routellm | arXiv title search: reasoning router

title: MESS+: Dynamically Learned Inference-Time LLM Routing in Model Zoos with Service Level Guarantees
cost_reduction_reported: Average 2x cost savings vs existing LLM routing techniques (abstract)
summary: MESS+ is a stochastic-optimization router for model zoos that learns satisfaction probabilities online and solves per-request optimization with virtual queues to meet SLA quality guarantees while minimizing cost. Includes theory on cost optimality and constraint satisfaction.
key_idea: Lyapunov-style virtual queues for SLA-guaranteed cost-optimal routing.
relevance_rationale: SLA framing matches enterprise needs.

title: From Deferral to Learning: Online In-Context Knowledge Distillation for LLM Cascades
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 33.06% weak-model and 6.35% system accuracy gain; up to 48.05% fewer strong-model calls and up to 49.63% fee savings vs standard cascades
summary: When the strong model resolves a deferred query, it also writes a reusable strategy that is stored and retrieved for similar future queries to help the weak model. The cascade thus learns online without fine-tuning.
key_idea: Strong model acts as an in-context teacher; stored strategies reduce future deferrals.
relevance_rationale: Online learning from live traffic inside a cascade.
found_via: arXiv search: "LLM cascade" | snowball: cited-by belcak-2025-slms-future-agentic-ai | snowball: cited-by nie-2024-online-cascade

title: Efficient Training-Free Online Routing for High-Volume Multi-LLM Serving
cost_reduction_reported: Average 3.55x improvement in overall performance, 1.85x in cost efficiency and ~4.25x throughput vs 8 baselines (abstract)
summary: Presents the first training-free algorithm for online routing under high query volume and token budgets, estimating query features via ANN search and solving a one-time optimization on initial queries. Provides a 1-o(1) competitive ratio guarantee.
key_idea: Online budgeted routing with competitive-ratio guarantees.
relevance_rationale: Theory for online budget-constrained routing.

title: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
cost_reduction_reported: Reported as over 8x more compute-efficient than baselines when scaling test-time compute
summary: Redefines PRMs for agent tasks: instead of step correctness, it scores each step's promise (proximity to goal) and progress, capturing interdependence between sequential decisions. Labels are obtained scalably with TD-based estimation combined with GAE; experiments cover agentic tasks such as web shopping and browser navigation.
key_idea: Agent PRM scoring promise and progress per step, trained with TD/GAE labels.
relevance_rationale: Cheap step-level scorer for agent trajectories, supports test-time compute allocation.
found_via: WebSearch: process reward model for LLM agents AgentPRM

title: Reducing Cost of LLM Agents with Trajectory Reduction
cost_reduction_reported: input tokens reduced 39.9%-59.7% and total computational cost reduced 21.1%-35.9% while maintaining agent performance
summary: AgentDiet removes useless, redundant and expired information from coding-agent trajectories at inference time, using a cheaper reflection model over a sliding window. It cuts input tokens and total cost substantially with no loss in resolve rate.
key_idea: Prune waste from growing agent trajectories during execution.
relevance_rationale: Context-level cost lever for long-horizon agents; uses a cheaper model for the reduction step.
found_via: web search: model switching mid-trajectory | SWE-agent context management trajectory reduction cost coding agents arXiv

title: Generalized Correctness Models: Learning Calibrated and Model-Agnostic Correctness Predictors from Historical Patterns
summary: Trains correctness predictors on historical correctness data across many models and finds they generalize across models, suggesting confidence estimation is learnable from history rather than self-introspection.
key_idea: Model-agnostic correctness predictors from logged outcomes.
relevance_rationale: Predict success of any model from historical logs, key for routers.

title: BOAD: Discovering Hierarchical Software Engineering Agents via Bandit Optimization
summary: Discovers a hierarchical SWE agent by treating candidate sub-agents as bandit arms whose reward is their helpfulness when collaborating, allowing efficient exploration under limited evaluation budgets. The discovered 36B system ranked second on SWE-bench Live at evaluation time.
key_idea: Multi-armed bandit search over sub-agent designs for hierarchical agents.
relevance_rationale: Bandit-driven agent configuration search with credit to sub-agents.

title: TRINITY: An Evolved LLM Coordinator
summary: Trinity uses a ~0.6B coordinator plus a ~10K-parameter head, optimized with separable CMA-ES, that at each turn assigns a Thinker, Worker or Verifier role to a chosen LLM. It beats individual models and prior methods, reaching 86.2% on LiveCodeBench.
key_idea: Tiny evolved coordinator assigns roles and models per turn.
relevance_rationale: Per-turn role+model assignment by a small coordinator; quality-focused rather than cost-focused.

title: Verification-Aware Planning for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: VeriMAP's planner decomposes tasks, models dependencies and writes verification functions for each subtask, so executors can be checked and retried. Because executors get well-scoped subtasks, cheaper models can execute them, partly offsetting planner cost.
key_idea: Planner writes per-subtask verifiers so executors can be smaller.

summary: ShapleyFlow applies cooperative game theory to attribute contributions of workflow components and identify task-specific component configurations, including different LLMs per component, that beat single-LLM workflows across 7 scenarios.

cost_reduction_reported: up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy translating into up to 20% latency reduction
summary: Speculative Actions uses fast models to guess an agent's next actions and executes them in parallel, committing only when the main model agrees, analogous to speculative decoding. It gives lossless latency savings and analyzes the cost-latency trade-off of speculative breadth.

cost_reduction_reported: Reduces cost on average by up to 86% more than state of the art across 8 real-world datasets, with stronger accuracy guarantees

summary: Model-SAT builds capability instructions from a model's aptitude-test results and trains a lightweight LLM to predict whether each candidate can handle an instruction. New models are onboarded by running a quick 50-task aptitude test, without candidate inference at routing time.

relevance_rationale: MAS pruning with heterogeneous-deployment cost results.

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
summary: A systematic evaluation of five multi-agent debate methods on nine benchmarks finds they often fail to beat CoT and self-consistency despite using more compute. Mixing heterogeneous models consistently improves MAD.

cost_reduction_reported: Accuracy 0.8390 vs 0.8272 for thinking-only, with 36.8% lower inference time and 39.66% fewer tokens on medical datasets

summary: Defines automated failure attribution for LLM multi-agent systems: identify the responsible agent and the decisive error step in a failed trace. Releases the Who&When dataset (failure logs from 127 MAS); the best method reaches 53.5% agent accuracy but only 14.2% step accuracy.
