title: Agent Workflow Memory
cost_reduction_reported: 24.6% and 51.1% relative success-rate improvement on Mind2Web and WebArena, with fewer steps taken on successful WebArena tasks
summary: AWM induces reusable routines (workflows) from agent trajectories, offline from training examples or online from test queries, and adds the relevant ones to the agent's memory to guide later tasks. It improves success and reduces the number of steps needed.
key_idea: Induce and reuse workflows so agents solve recurring tasks in fewer steps.
relevance_rationale: Workflow reuse lowers per-task steps (and hence calls); a basis for plan caching.

title: Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies
summary: Argues reasoning strategies should be compared at matched compute; with equal budgets, CoT self-consistency often beats more complex strategies, and multi-agent debate or Reflexion can get worse with more budget.
key_idea: Budget-aware evaluation of reasoning strategies.
relevance_rationale: Evaluation principle for multi-agent cost claims.
found_via: arXiv title search: token budget reasoning

title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
summary: Re-examines whether multi-agent discussion improves LLM reasoning and finds that a single agent with strong prompts (demonstrations) matches the best discussion frameworks across tasks and backbones. Multi-agent discussion only helps when no demonstrations are given.
key_idea: A well-prompted single agent matches multi-agent discussion.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence on when multi-agent architecture is not worth its extra calls.

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
cost_reduction_reported: $0.70 per issue at 32.00% on SWE-bench Lite, highest among open-source agents at the time
summary: Agentless replaces an autonomous coding agent with a fixed three-phase pipeline (localize, repair, validate) and reaches the best open-source SWE-bench Lite result at the time at about $0.70 per issue. It questions whether complex agent loops are needed for many software tasks.
key_idea: A fixed simple pipeline can beat complex agents on cost and accuracy.
relevance_rationale: Key architecture-level cost evidence: workflow vs agent.

title: Which LLM to Play? Convergence-Aware Online Model Selection with Time-Increasing Bandits
models_studied: API LLMs vs fine-tuned small LLMs
summary: Studies online model selection when candidate models improve over time (e.g. a small model being fine-tuned), using a time-increasing bandit (TI-UCB) with change detection for convergence. Proves logarithmic regret and tests on classification and LLM selection.
key_idea: Increasing-then-converging bandit for choosing between costly API LLM and improving local model.
relevance_rationale: Directly models the API-vs-local-small-model decision under online learning.
found_via: OpenAlex title: online model selection LLM

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
summary: Simulated small software company with internal websites, data and simulated coworkers, where agents browse, code, run programs and communicate. The best baseline agent completes 30% of tasks autonomously.
key_idea: Digital-worker benchmark with consequential multi-tool tasks.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise-like long-horizon digital-worker tasks.

title: EcoAct: Economic Agent Determines When to Register What Action
cost_reduction_reported: Over 50% reduction in computational cost on multi-step reasoning tasks while maintaining performance
summary: EcoAct gives the agent a single meta-tool to register tools on demand from their names, instead of loading all tool descriptions into context every step. Integrating tool registration into reasoning cuts cost by more than half on multi-step tasks without hurting accuracy.
key_idea: Register tools lazily inside the reasoning loop to shrink per-step context.
relevance_rationale: Seed; step-level tool-context cost lever.

title: Scaling LLM Inference with Optimized Sample Compute Allocation
cost_reduction_reported: Beats best single configuration with 128x less compute on code generation and 25x less on 4 reasoning tasks; better SWE-Bench accuracy with 3x less compute than default configuration
summary: Learns an optimal mix of sampling configurations (model, temperature, language) and sample counts under a compute budget, including for an agentic SWE workflow.
key_idea: Optimise the mixture of inference configurations under budget.
relevance_rationale: Configuration optimisation across models including agent tasks.
found_via: snowball: related work of snell-2024-test-time-compute-optimal | search: LLM configuration tuning inference hyperparameters optimization arXiv

title: Efficient Contextual LLM Cascades through Budget-Constrained Policy Learning
cost_reduction_reported: Cost savings of up to 85% compared to baselines while maintaining high accuracy
summary: TREACLE is an RL policy that jointly picks the model and prompt scheme for each question under long-run monetary and latency budgets. It uses question embeddings and the consistency of previous responses as state.
key_idea: Budget-constrained RL policy over (model, prompt) choices with re-query ability.
relevance_rationale: Cascade as sequential decision process under budget.
found_via: arXiv search: "LLM cascade" | OpenAlex title search

title: Eagle: Efficient Training-Free Router for Multi-LLM Inference
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 23.52% AUC improvement; 1/20 of baseline initialization time and 100-200x faster incremental updates (abstract)
summary: Eagle is a training-free router combining global ELO rankings with local ELO computed over similar past queries. It improves routing AUC and supports very fast incremental updates for high-volume online serving.
key_idea: Training-free ELO-based routing with fast online updates.
relevance_rationale: Cheap to maintain in production.
found_via: snowball: cited-by ong-2024-routellm | OpenAlex title search

title: LoRA Land: 310 Fine-tuned LLMs that Rival GPT-4, A Technical Report
cost_reduction_reported: 4-bit LoRA fine-tuned models beat base models by 34 points and GPT-4 by 10 points on average; 25 LoRA Mistral-7B models served on one A100
summary: Predibase technical report evaluating 310 LoRA fine-tuned models across 10 base models and 31 tasks, and LoRAX serving of many adapters on a single GPU (LoRA Land app).
key_idea: Many small task-specific LoRAs beat GPT-4 and can be served cheaply together.
relevance_rationale: Industry evidence on specialization plus multi-adapter serving economics.

title: EmbedLLM: Learning Compact Representations of Large Language Models
summary: EmbedLLM learns compact vector representations of LLMs with an encoder-decoder trained on query-level correctness data. The embeddings support routing and forecasting benchmark performance without running the model, and outperform prior methods on routing accuracy and latency.
key_idea: Matrix-factorization-style LLM embeddings reused across routing and performance prediction.
relevance_rationale: Scalable model representation for routing over large and changing pools.
found_via: seed | OpenAlex title search | seed: EmbedLLM

title: Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluate Agents with Agents
summary: Proposes using agentic systems (with tools to inspect workspaces and traces) to judge other agents, giving intermediate feedback over the whole task process. Introduces DevAI, 55 AI-development tasks with 365 hierarchical requirements, and finds Agent-as-a-Judge is far more reliable than LLM-as-a-Judge and comparable to human evaluators.
key_idea: Use an agent with tools as the evaluator of agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Provides a ground-truth-free trajectory quality signal; the paper also reports large cost/time savings versus human evaluation.

title: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces computational cost by over 50% for comparable performance (five LMs, five datasets)
summary: AutoMix lets a small model answer, estimates correctness through few-shot self-verification, and uses a POMDP-based router to decide whether to escalate to larger models given noisy verification. Across five models and datasets it cuts cost by over half at comparable quality.
key_idea: Self-verification plus POMDP escalation policy.
relevance_rationale: Widely cited cascade/router hybrid with a sequential decision formulation.
found_via: snowball: related work of ding-2024-hybrid-llm | seed: AutoMix | keyword: self-verification routing

title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
cost_reduction_reported: Fine-tuning Llama2-7B on 500 GPT-4 agent trajectories gives a 77% HotpotQA performance increase; paper discusses cost/efficiency gains versus prompting
summary: Fine-tunes smaller LMs on GPT-4-generated ReAct-style agent trajectories across multiple tasks and prompting methods, showing large gains in accuracy, robustness and efficiency versus few-shot prompting.
key_idea: Fine-tune small agents on teacher trajectories instead of prompting large models.
relevance_rationale: Seminal agent distillation evidence with explicit cost/efficiency discussion.

title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
cost_reduction_reported: Matches best individual LLM (e.g. GPT-4) with up to 98% cost reduction, or +4% accuracy over GPT-4 at the same cost (abstract)
summary: Surveys cost reduction strategies for LLM APIs (prompt adaptation, LLM approximation, cascades) and proposes FrugalGPT, a learned cascade that decides which LLM combinations to query per input. It reports large cost reductions on classification-style tasks.
key_idea: Learned LLM cascade with a scorer deciding when to stop.
relevance_rationale: Foundational cost-reduction paper that framed routing/cascades for API LLMs.
found_via: snowball: related work of ong-2024-routellm | arXiv search: "LLM cascade"

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
cost_reduction_reported: Compiled DSPy programs on small open LMs (770M T5, llama2-13b-chat) are competitive with expert-written prompt chains for proprietary GPT-3.5
summary: Introduces DSPy, a programming model where LM pipelines are declarative modules with learnable prompts/demonstrations, plus a compiler that optimizes a whole pipeline toward a metric. Shows bootstrapped pipelines beat standard few-shot prompting and let small open models approach proprietary-model pipelines.
key_idea: Treat LM pipelines as parameterized programs and compile (optimize) prompts/demos end-to-end against a metric.
relevance_rationale: Foundational framework for optimizing compound AI pipelines; the cheaper-model-with-optimized-program result is a direct cost lever.

title: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling
cost_reduction_reported: up to 3.7x latency speedup, up to 6.7x cost savings and up to ~9% accuracy improvement vs ReAct; up to 1.35x latency gain over OpenAI parallel function calling
benchmarks: function-calling tasks with varied dependency patterns
summary: LLMCompiler plans function calls as a DAG and executes independent calls in parallel via a planner, task-fetching unit and executor, instead of ReAct-style sequential reasoning. It cuts latency and cost while improving accuracy.
key_idea: Compile agent tool calls into a parallel execution plan.
relevance_rationale: Architecture-level cost reduction for tool-using agents; complements config search.
found_via: seed: LLMCompiler | LLMCompiler parallel function calling

title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
summary: A dual-process agent pairs a small fine-tuned encoder-decoder that proposes actions quickly with a large LLM that is invoked for planning and grounding when heuristics signal trouble. The combination beats ReAct, Reflexion and SayCan on 30 ScienceWorld tasks while calling the expensive LLM less often.
key_idea: Small imitation-learned policy acts by default; a large LLM is called only when heuristics detect difficulty.
relevance_rationale: Canonical big-little switching inside an agent loop; directly analogous to per-step downscaling.

title: Routing to the Expert: Efficient Reward-guided Ensemble of Large Language Models
summary: Zooter distills reward-model scores on training queries into a routing function that sends each query to the LLM with relevant expertise, avoiding the cost of generating from every model and ranking. Tag-based label enhancement reduces noise from silver reward supervision; across 26 subsets it beats the best single model on average.
key_idea: Distill off-the-shelf reward-model rankings into a cheap pre-generation router.
relevance_rationale: Early reward-guided router showing routing can replace expensive output reranking.

title: Cache & Distil: Optimising API Calls to Large Language Models
signals_used: active-learning criteria (margin sampling, query by committee)
summary: Neural caching: a student model is continuously trained on LLM responses and a policy decides which requests the student handles alone. Margin sampling and query-by-committee policies work best.
key_idea: Online student distillation with active-learning deferral.
relevance_rationale: Distillation from production traffic with deferral.
found_via: snowball: related work of FrugalGPT (2305.05176) | OpenAlex title search

title: Fly-Swat or Cannon? Cost-Effective Language Model Choice via Meta-Modeling
cost_reduction_reported: match the performance of the largest LM while achieving a cost reduction of 63% (14 datasets, four LMs)
summary: A meta-model predicts how well each candidate LM will do on each input, then an assignment solves budget-constrained or cost-minimising allocation across a batch.
key_idea: Meta-model plus batch assignment for LM choice.
relevance_rationale: Early router; batch-assignment framing.
found_via: snowball: related work of cascade papers (verified on arXiv) | OpenAlex title search

title: Large Language Model Routing with Benchmark Datasets
summary: Recasts benchmark datasets as training data for a router that picks the best LLM for new tasks, reducing the problem to a collection of binary correctness classifiers. It shows consistent gains over any single model and discusses limits of transferring from benchmarks.
key_idea: Reuse benchmark outcomes to train per-model correctness predictors for routing.
relevance_rationale: Early principled formulation of learned routing from benchmark logs.
found_via: snowball: related work of ong-2024-routellm | OpenAlex title search

title: Cache me if you Can: an Online Cost-aware Teacher-Student framework to Reduce the Calls to Large Language Models
venue_or_source: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
cost_reduction_reported: Reports significant operating-expense savings with only slightly lower performance on intent recognition and sentiment analysis (GPT-3.5/GPT-4 teachers)
summary: Proposes an online teacher-student framework in which a cheap local model is trained on LLM responses as they arrive and gradually answers more queries itself, calling the LLM only when needed. Gives a method to tune the call criteria and measure the cost-performance trade-off on business classification tasks.
key_idea: Distill an LLM into a cheap student online from live calls and route to the student when it is confident.
relevance_rationale: Online learning from live traffic to cut LLM calls; directly applicable to repetitive enterprise subtasks.

title: Cost-Effective Hyperparameter Optimization for Large Language Model Generation Inference
summary: EcoOptiGen tunes LLM inference hyperparameters (number of responses, temperature, max tokens, prompts, model) under a budget using economical hyperparameter optimization with cost-based pruning; implemented in FLAML's autogen package.
key_idea: Budget-aware HPO of LLM inference hyperparameters.
relevance_rationale: Early cost-aware LLM inference config tuning, ancestor of AutoGen tuning.
found_via: search: LLM configuration tuning inference hyperparameters optimization arXiv

title: Large Language Model Cascades with Mixture of Thoughts Representations for Cost-efficient Reasoning
cost_reduction_reported: Performance comparable to GPT-4 alone at 40% of its cost (GPT-3.5-turbo as weak model), six reasoning benchmarks
summary: Uses the agreement among multiple sampled answers from a cheap LLM as a difficulty signal for escalating reasoning questions. Mixing chain-of-thought and program-of-thought samples makes the consistency check more discriminative.
key_idea: Answer consistency across mixed thought representations as a label-free deferral signal.
relevance_rationale: Seed; cheap, training-free escalation signal transferable to agent steps.
found_via: seed: Mixture-of-Thought cascades | keyword: self-consistency cost

title: EcoAssistant: Using LLM Assistant More Affordably and Accurately
cost_reduction_reported: Surpasses GPT-4 by 10 points of success rate with less than 50% of GPT-4's cost
summary: For code-driven assistant queries, tries cheaper LLMs first with an execution loop and backs off to stronger ones, and retrieves solutions from past successful queries as demonstrations.
key_idea: Assistant hierarchy plus solution retrieval for agentic code queries.
relevance_rationale: Early cascade for tool-using assistants.
found_via: snowball: related work of cascade papers (verified on arXiv)

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
cost_reduction_reported: up to 6.4x higher throughput than state-of-the-art inference systems on agent control, reasoning, few-shot, JSON decoding, RAG and multi-turn chat
summary: SGLang pairs a frontend language for LLM programs (generation and parallelism primitives) with a runtime featuring RadixAttention, which keeps KV caches in a radix tree for automatic prefix reuse across calls, and compressed finite-state machines for fast structured decoding. The LMSYS blog (lmsys.org/blog/2024-01-17-sglang) introduced RadixAttention.
key_idea: Co-design a program frontend with a runtime that reuses KV prefixes automatically.
relevance_rationale: Prefix reuse across the many calls of an agent program is a major serving cost lever.

title: About Copilot auto model selection
cost_reduction_reported: (vendor-reported) 10% discount on model costs when using auto selection on paid plans
summary: Copilot's auto mode combines a system that tracks model health and availability with one that estimates task complexity, and switches models at natural cache boundaries or large complexity shifts in a conversation, subject to admin policies.
key_idea: Cache-boundary-aware model switching in a coding assistant.
relevance_rationale: Production router explicitly aligning switches with cache boundaries.

title: Auto Router (Intelligent Model Selection)
summary: OpenRouter's free auto router classifies each prompt into about 30 task types, ranks models by what the OpenRouter community actually spends on for that task over the last seven days, applies the user's cost tier, and returns primary picks with fallbacks and session stickiness. The current docs describe this market-signal design and do not mention Not Diamond (earlier versions were reported as Not Diamond-powered, unverified here).
key_idea: Route by aggregate market spend per task type.
relevance_rationale: Production router using live aggregate traffic as signal.

title: COMED: The Missing Middle Between Routing and Collaboration in Multi-LLM Inference
summary: COMED escalates to cross-model collaboration only when a post-anchor controller predicts rescued errors outweigh harms, improving routed anchors while using fewer calls than dense collaboration.
key_idea: Selective escalation between routing and full collaboration.
relevance_rationale: Selective multi-model use.

title: Compaction overview (Claude Platform docs)
summary: Documents server-side compaction, where the API replaces older turns with a model-written summary either on demand or when input tokens cross a configured trigger, optionally keeping recent turns verbatim and running in the background. It contrasts this with client-side summarizers and with rule-based context editing.
key_idea: Provider-managed summarization of history keeps long agent tasks within a small active context.
relevance_rationale: Directly usable context-cost mechanism for long-horizon agents; no numbers.

title: Effort (Claude Platform docs)
summary: Describes output_config.effort, which controls how many tokens Claude spends (thinking, text and tool calls) on a single model, from low up to max; most models default to high while Opus 5.5 defaults to medium. A per-message effort setting is in beta, allowing effort to vary across turns of an agent loop, and effort is the recommended control for thinking depth where adaptive thinking is available.
key_idea: Single-model effort levels, settable per message, as a substitute for switching models to save cost.
relevance_rationale: Per-step effort control is a direct alternative lever to step-level model routing.

title: RPRA: Predicting an LLM-Judge for Efficient but Performant Inference
summary: Models predict, before answering, how an LLM judge would score their output, and defer when the prediction is low. Report cards in context and fine-tuning improve small models' prediction accuracy by up to 55% and 52%.
key_idea: Predict your own judge score to decide deferral.
relevance_rationale: Self-assessment as deferral signal.
found_via: arXiv search: learning to defer LLM

title: Federate the Router: Learning Language Model Routers with Sparse and Decentralized Evaluations
summary: Introduces federated learning of LLM routers so clients with private, sparse query-model evaluations can learn a shared routing policy.
key_idea: Federated router training across clients.
relevance_rationale: Relevant for multi-tenant enterprise data.

title: Pioneer Agent: Continual Improvement of Small Language Models in Production
summary: Pioneer Agent automates the lifecycle of specializing small models for production: data acquisition, evaluation set construction, training, and in production mode diagnosing labeled failures and retraining under regression constraints. It raises intent classification from 84.9% to 99.3% in a production-style deployment.
key_idea: Agent that continually specializes SLMs from production failures.
relevance_rationale: Supports replacing frontier calls with continually improved SLMs.
found_via: arXiv title search: small language models agentic

title: AgentBetta: Verification-Driven Adaptive Configuration of an AI Nano-Agent through Selective Expansion and Verified Contraction
cost_reduction_reported: Median context allocation reduced from 64,000 to 8,000 characters and tool exposure from five to zero at 91.38% verified success on AB-ConfigBench
summary: AgentBetta treats an agent's model capability, context, tools, permissions and memory as an executable configuration. It starts minimal, expands selectively when verification diagnoses a deficiency, and contracts counterfactually after success.
key_idea: Verification-driven expand/contract of agent configuration, including model capability.
relevance_rationale: Adaptive per-task resource provisioning for agents.

title: LLM Performance Predictors: Learning When to Escalate in Hybrid Human-AI Moderation Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Significant improvements in accuracy-cost trade-offs over existing uncertainty estimators (no single number in abstract)
summary: Trains a meta-model on LLM performance predictors derived from outputs to decide when to automate moderation decisions and when to escalate to humans. Also gives explanations of failure conditions.
key_idea: Supervised meta-model on output features for when-to-escalate decisions.
relevance_rationale: Escalation to humans in real moderation workflows.

title: Closing the Operational Gap in Semantic Caching
summary: Shows that offline ranking metrics (e.g., PR-AUC) poorly predict how a similarity model performs once a threshold is fixed in a deployed semantic cache. Proposes a precision-vs-cache-hit-ratio AUC and an operational retention rate, and argues that model selection is a threshold-utility problem.
key_idea: Evaluate semantic-cache models at deployment thresholds, not by offline ranking.
relevance_rationale: Evaluation methodology for cache correctness/cost tradeoff.

title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
summary: Releases 115 manually annotated failed trajectories spanning API workflows, incident management and open-ended tasks, and AgentRx, an automated framework that pinpoints the critical failure step.
key_idea: Automated critical-step diagnosis for agent failures.
relevance_rationale: Failure diagnosis incl. incident-management workloads.

title: Continual Model Routing in Evolving Model Hubs
summary: Formalizes continual model routing as model hubs grow, releases CMRBench with over 2,000 candidates, and proposes CARvE contrastive embeddings with replay.
key_idea: Continual routing over growing model hubs.
relevance_rationale: Pool growth.

title: Online Pandora's Box for Contextual LLM Cascading
summary: Formulates contextual LLM cascading as an online Pandora's Box problem where each API query reveals an output at a cost and only the deployed output's reward is observed. Learns reservation indices with GMM estimation plus UCB bounds and proves sqrt(T) regret.
key_idea: Weitzman-index cascading learned online with bandit feedback.
relevance_rationale: Theory for online cascade learning from traffic.

title: Marginal-Contribution Policy Gradients under Filtered Feedback for Multi-Agent LLMs
summary: Proves that shared-reward training of multi-agent LLM systems cannot distinguish agents that matter from ones that do not, and derives gradient-correct marginal-contribution signals identifiable from filtered feedback, with an optimal budget for exact counterfactual evaluations. In GRPO it improves routed GSM8K over winner-take-all training at no extra generation cost.
key_idea: Marginal-contribution credit assignment for routed multi-agent LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Credit assignment theory applicable to deciding which agents matter (sub-theme f).
found_via: arXiv query abs:"credit assignment" AND abs:"multi-agent" AND abs:"LLM" AND abs:cost

title: An Exact Generate - Transform Decomposition of Small-LLM Team Scaling Across Orchestration Architectures
cost_reduction_reported: At equal call budgets token cost still varies 2.1x across architectures
summary: Sweeps eight orchestration architectures with 7-9B models up to 30 calls and finds team-scaling returns are sharply task-dependent: large on arithmetic, small on multiple-choice. An exact generate-transform decomposition explains which architectures convert extra candidates into accuracy.
key_idea: Team scaling is a task- and architecture-specific bet.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on the value of adding agents.

title: TokenDance: Scaling Multi-Agent LLM Serving via Collective KV Cache Sharing
cost_reduction_reported: up to 2.7x more concurrent agents than vLLM prefix caching under SLO, per-agent KV storage reduced up to 17.5x, up to 1.9x prefill speedup
summary: Scales many-agent simulations by sharing KV blocks collectively and storing sibling agents' caches as block-sparse diffs against a master copy.
key_idea: Collective KV sharing with diff-compressed sibling caches.
relevance_rationale: Serving many agents cheaply on shared context.
found_via: Tokencake KV cache multi-agent function call serving

title: Sutradhara: An Intelligent Orchestrator-Engine Co-design for Tool-based Agentic Inference
cost_reduction_reported: sustains up to 77% higher load at the same median first-token-response latency, or up to 15% lower median latency at the same load, and up to 11% lower end-to-end latency on A100
summary: Co-designs the agent orchestrator and the vLLM engine: tool-aware prompt splitting, streaming tool dispatch during decode, and orchestrator-informed cache management.
key_idea: Orchestrator-engine co-design for tool-based agents.
relevance_rationale: Tool-aware agent serving.

title: What Stops a Small Language Model From Driving a Database Agent
summary: Over eleven days the authors drove a real open-source SQL client's agent mode with 39 local open-weight models (8,199 runs). Most small-model losses came from runs that did call tools, mostly transport/argument-shape failures, and five server-side fixes moved model results substantially without changing any model.
key_idea: Small-model agent failures are often interface failures, not capability gaps.
relevance_rationale: Practical evidence on making SLMs viable inside agents.

title: Do Small Language Models Know When They're Wrong? Confidence-Based Cascade Scoring for Educational Assessment
cost_reduction_reported: Best cascade approached large-LM accuracy (kappa 0.802 vs 0.819) at 76% lower cost and 61% lower latency
summary: Evaluates verbalised confidence as the escalation signal for educational scoring cascades. Confidence discrimination varies widely across small models and is the bottleneck.
key_idea: Discrimination of verbalised confidence determines cascade value.
relevance_rationale: Practical evaluation of confidence-based escalation.
found_via: arXiv title search: cascades language models

title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
summary: Shows how to spend a limited budget for expert reward annotation in sequential OPE when cheap LLM-judge labels are biased, using doubly robust OPE with missing rewards and variance-optimal annotation probabilities. Motivated by casenotes from a homelessness services nonprofit.
key_idea: Variance-optimal choice of which logged steps to label expertly for doubly robust OPE.
relevance_rationale: Label-budget allocation for evaluating logged policies when rewards come from judges.

title: CoACT: Action-Preserving Observation Compression for Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: average total token consumption reduced 33.0% on SWE-bench Verified with near-uncompressed task success
summary: A teacher generates compressed candidates of each observation; candidates that would change the agent's next action are filtered out, and the shortest remaining ones supervise a lightweight observation compressor.
key_idea: Train a small compressor that keeps the agent's next action unchanged.
relevance_rationale: Action-preserving observation compression; distillation of a compressor.

title: An Empirical Cost Attribution of Context-Compression Gateways in Multi-Turn Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Tool-schema filtering removes ~21K-57K tokens per turn; content compression saves only ~2% of cache-priced prefix per turn (real Claude Code/Codex sessions)
summary: Instruments a production compression gateway between coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) and frontier LLMs and decomposes the token bill into tool-schema filtering, content compression and history summarization under controlled A/B runs. Only schema filtering is reliably positive once prompt caching is priced in.
key_idea: With prompt caching, compression savings are much smaller than benchmarks imply.
relevance_rationale: Production cost attribution for coding agents; supporting lever.
found_via: Semantic Scholar query "per-turn model routing coding agent"

title: CONCUR: High-Throughput Agentic Batch Inference of LLM via Congestion-Based Concurrency Control
cost_reduction_reported: batch inference throughput up to 4.09x on Qwen3-32B and 1.9x on DeepSeek-V3
summary: Congestion-control-style admission for agentic batch inference: dynamically adjusts how many agents are active based on cache signals to avoid KV thrashing in the middle of runs.
key_idea: Admission control for agents to prevent cache thrashing.
relevance_rationale: Batch/offline agent workloads efficiency.

title: A Component-Based Survey of Interactions between Large Language Models and Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Survey of how bandit algorithms help LLM systems (from pretraining to RAG and personalization) and how LLMs help bandits, organized by component; with a curated GitHub list.
key_idea: Component-level survey of LLM-bandit interactions.
relevance_rationale: Useful map of bandit methods applied to LLMs.

title: Outcome-Aware Tool Selection for Semantic Routers: Latency-Constrained Learning Without LLM Inference
summary: OATS improves tool selection in semantic routers at LLM gateways by shifting tool embeddings toward the centroid of queries where each tool historically succeeded, an offline step that adds no serving latency. NDCG@5 on MetaTool rises from 0.869 to 0.940; learned re-rankers help only when outcome data is plentiful.
key_idea: Learn tool routing from historical outcomes offline with zero serving cost.
relevance_rationale: Learning routing from logged outcomes in gateways.

title: Resample or Reroute? Recoverable Stopping Debt Without Identified Action Selection
cost_reduction_reported: In a 152-query MBPP+ study, fixed escalation to Qwen2.5-14B exceeds leave-one-out 7B resampling by +2.882 pp after 7B rejection
summary: Treats choosing between resampling and rerouting after a weak verifier as an identification problem because correctness is hidden, and orders three gates (recoverable stopping debt, action support, held-out selector value) that must pass before claiming a learned selector helps.
key_idea: Gated identification test before claiming a resample-vs-reroute selector adds value.
relevance_rationale: Rigorous treatment of counterfactual claims in escalation decisions.

title: What Does a Routing Oracle Measure Under Stochastic Decoding? Coupling, Scorer Choice, and Single-Commit Ceilings
summary: Shows that the hindsight oracle used in routing benchmarks is not the same decision class as a router that commits to one model before seeing outputs under stochastic decoding. Distinguishes single-commit ceilings from union probabilities and audits frozen correctness tensors from 11 models.
key_idea: Routing oracles under stochastic decoding overstate the achievable gain of single-commit routers.
relevance_rationale: Clarifies what can be identified when learning or evaluating routers from logged outcomes.

title: Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics
summary: A survey framing tokens as economic production factors for agents, organized into single-agent budget control, multi-agent collaboration friction, ecosystem pricing and security. Useful framing for cost-aware agent design.

summary: Finds an ellipsis in the prompt stochastically toggles thinking in R1-style models, then uses multi-stage RL with reward shaping to invoke explicit reasoning only when needed.
key_idea: Exploit latent think/no-think controllability with staged RL.
relevance_rationale: Adaptive thinking for R1-style models.

title: Token-Level Truth: Real-Time Hallucination Detection for Production LLMs (HaluGate)
cost_reduction_reported: Pre-classification skips detection for non-factual queries, a 72.2% efficiency gain where ~35% of queries are non-factual; detection ~125ms for typical RAG context, ~365ms at 16K tokens (project-reported)
summary: HaluGate is a conditional pipeline in the vLLM Semantic Router: a small classifier (96.4% validation accuracy, ~12ms) decides whether a response needs fact-checking, then a token-level detector plus an NLI explainer flag unsupported spans against tool/RAG context, with results surfaced in response headers. Token-level detection alone reached only 59% F1, which motivated the ensemble.
key_idea: Cheap gated, non-LLM verifiers can provide per-response quality signals at the gateway without an LLM judge.
relevance_rationale: Low-cost quality signal usable as an escalation trigger in routing.

title: vLLM Semantic Router: Next Phase in LLM inference

summary: Open-source router (Red Hat, IBM Research, Tencent contributors) that classifies intent with a ModernBERT classifier and chooses a fast path or chain-of-thought reasoning path and a model, deployed on Kubernetes. Claims lack disclosed methodology; an independent evaluation found no task-specific advantage over blind allocation.
key_idea: Classifier-based reasoning-mode and model selection in the serving layer.
relevance_rationale: Widely adopted OSS router; independent evaluation is skeptical.

title: DRIFT: Learning from Abundant User Dissatisfaction in Real-World Preference Learning
summary: Observes that deployments produce abundant implicit dissatisfaction signals (users refining or correcting) but few explicit positives, and proposes DRIFT, which anchors preference training on dissatisfaction examples and samples positives from the evolving policy. Reports up to +7.61% WildBench task score and +12.29% AlpacaEval2 win rate at 14B over base models.
key_idea: Learn from plentiful dissatisfaction signals in real logs instead of scarce positive labels.
relevance_rationale: Shows how regenerations and corrections in production logs become a usable learning signal.

cost_reduction_reported: Up to 90% lower end-to-end latency with accuracy within +/-1% of dense MoA
summary: Co-designs MoA serving with a tree topology for sparse communication, runtime skipping of downstream agents based on agreement and confidence, and overlapping prefill with decode across dependent agents. Latency drops sharply at near-equal accuracy.
key_idea: Sparse tree MoA with confidence-based agent skipping and pipelined serving.
relevance_rationale: Serving-level MoA efficiency.

title: Entropy After </Think> for reasoning model early exiting
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces token usage by 12-22% without harming accuracy on MATH500 and AIME2025; works black-box via proxy models (Llama 70B with 1.5B proxy, Claude 3.7 with 4B proxy)
summary: Appends a stop-thinking token and tracks the entropy of the next token; when its moving variance stabilises, reasoning is stopped. Can run with a small proxy for black-box models.
key_idea: Cheap entropy signal for stopping reasoning, even for API models.
relevance_rationale: Black-box-compatible early exit.

title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
summary: Cognition (Devin) argues from production agent-building experience that parallel multi-agent decompositions are fragile because subagents lack shared context and make conflicting implicit decisions. Claude Code's read-only subagents and edit-apply models are discussed as examples.
key_idea: Context sharing, not agent count, determines reliability; prefer single-threaded agents plus history compression over parallel subagents.
relevance_rationale: Widely cited practitioner position on when multi-agent architectures are not worth it; qualitative, no numbers.

relevance_rationale: Prefix reuse at cluster scale for agent/system-prompt-heavy traffic.
found_via: Preble prefix-aware scheduling distributed LLM serving

title: WorkBench: a Benchmark Dataset for Agents in a Realistic Workplace Setting
summary: Workplace sandbox with five databases, 26 tools and 690 tasks such as emailing and scheduling, graded by unique database outcomes. ReAct agents completed between 3% and 43% of tasks and sometimes took harmful wrong actions.
key_idea: Outcome-based workplace task evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise-style benchmark.

title: Teola: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications
cost_reduction_reported: up to 2.09x speedup over existing systems across popular LLM applications
summary: Teola represents each query's workflow as a fine-grained dataflow graph of task primitives (spanning LLM, retrieval and other modules) and optimizes parallelism, pipelining and scheduling end to end. Its code lives in the Ayo repository.
key_idea: Fine-grained primitive-level orchestration of LLM applications.
relevance_rationale: End-to-end optimization of compound pipelines.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
summary: A controllable world of 9 everyday apps with 457 APIs and about 100 simulated users, and a benchmark of 750 tasks requiring interactive code generation, graded by state-based tests that also detect collateral damage. GPT-4o solves about 49% of normal and 30% of challenge tasks.
key_idea: API-rich simulated app world with collateral-damage checks.
relevance_rationale: Tool-use agent benchmark used in agent-efficiency studies.

title: Cascade-Aware Training of Language Models
summary: Trains the small model of a cascade with awareness of its position and of the large model downstream, rather than training models independently. Improves the overall quality-cost trade-off over 60+ tasks.
key_idea: Train the small model for its role in the cascade.
relevance_rationale: Training-side lever for cascades; relevant to specialising cheap agents.
found_via: arXiv title search: cascading language models

title: Make Every Penny Count: Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency for Cost-Efficient Reasoning
cost_reduction_reported: Consistently surpasses ASC and ESC in cost by a significant margin at comparable performance (six benchmarks)
summary: Uses difficulty estimates for batches of queries to allocate self-consistency samples, avoiding repeated sampling on easy questions.
key_idea: Difficulty-aware sample allocation.
relevance_rationale: Budget allocation across queries.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking) | hf-papers search: self-consistency cost efficient adaptive

title: Learning From Failure: Integrating Negative Examples when Fine-tuning Large Language Models as Agents
summary: Shows including failed GPT-4 trajectories (with negative-aware prompts) when fine-tuning smaller agents improves results over discarding them.
key_idea: Use failed teacher trajectories in agent SFT.
relevance_rationale: Production logs contain many failures; this shows how to use them.

title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
cost_reduction_reported: MoA-Lite reported as more cost-effective than GPT-4o with a 1.8% AlpacaEval 2.0 quality gain (per search summary of the paper)
summary: Layers of LLM agents each consume the previous layer's outputs and an aggregator synthesizes the final response; an all-open-source MoA reaches 65.1% on AlpacaEval 2.0 versus 57.5% for GPT-4 Omni. A lighter MoA-Lite configuration trades some quality for lower cost.
key_idea: Stack proposer LLMs in layers with an aggregator to exceed a single frontier model.
relevance_rationale: Heterogeneous multi-model composition; baseline for cost-aware MoA variants.

title: Navigating the LLM Landscape: Uber's Innovation with GenAI Gateway
summary: Uber's internal OpenAI-compatible gateway unifies external and self-hosted models with PII redaction, auth, audit logs for cost attribution and quality evaluation; about 30 teams and 16M queries per month at the time.
key_idea: Central gateway for multi-vendor access and cost attribution.
relevance_rationale: Production gateway at scale; foundation for routing.

title: Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Llemma-7B with the proposed tree search consistently outperforms Llemma-34B across tested inference strategies on MATH
summary: Empirical study of compute-optimal inference across model sizes and strategies (greedy, voting, best-of-n, tree search), finding smaller models with better inference algorithms are often Pareto-optimal.
key_idea: Small model plus smart inference can be compute-optimal.
relevance_rationale: Guides size vs test-time compute choices.

title: OCEAN: Offline Chain-of-thought Evaluation and Alignment in Large Language Models
summary: OCEAN performs offline evaluation of chain-of-thought using knowledge-graph feedback and a KG-IPS estimator with unbiasedness guarantees, then optimizes the LLM off-policy.
key_idea: IPS-based offline evaluation of LLM reasoning paths.
relevance_rationale: Shows IPS/OPE adapted to LLM outputs.

title: AgentGym: Evolving Large Language Model-based Agents across Diverse Environments
summary: Provides a framework of diverse environments, a trajectory set (AgentTraj) and AgentEvol, a self-evolution method letting agents improve beyond imitation across environments.
key_idea: Environments plus self-evolution for generalist agents.
relevance_rationale: Infrastructure for training small agents.

title: Watch Every Step! LLM Agent Learning via Iterative Step-Level Process Refinement
summary: Iterative step-level process refinement: step rewards estimated via Monte Carlo guide contrastive action pairs for agent training.
key_idea: Step-level rewards to refine agent training.
relevance_rationale: Links step signals to specialization.

title: Conveyor: Efficient Tool-aware LLM Serving with Tool Partial Execution
cost_reduction_reported: tool partial execution improves request completion latency by up to 38.8%
summary: Lets tools start executing on partial LLM output during decoding via an interface for tool developers and a scheduler that overlaps tool work with generation.
key_idea: Start tool execution before the LLM finishes emitting the call.
relevance_rationale: Tool-call-aware serving reduces agent latency.

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
cost_reduction_reported: time-to-first-token reduced 2.2-3.3x and throughput increased 2.8-5x vs full KV recompute without compromising quality
summary: For RAG inputs made of several precomputed chunks, CacheBlend reuses each chunk's KV cache and recomputes only a small subset of tokens whose KV values deviate most, restoring cross-chunk attention cheaply and overlapping recompute with KV loading.
key_idea: Selective KV recompute makes non-prefix KV cache reuse accurate.
relevance_rationale: KV reuse for retrieval/tool-context chunks that recur across agent calls.
found_via: CacheBlend fast LLM serving RAG cached knowledge fusion

title: EvoAgent: Towards Automatic Multi-Agent Generation via Evolutionary Algorithms
summary: EvoAgent treats an existing agent framework as an initial individual and applies evolutionary operators (mutation, crossover, selection) to generate diverse expert agents, extending single agents into multi-agent systems without manual design.
key_idea: Evolutionary expansion of a single agent into a multi-agent system.
relevance_rationale: Automated multi-agent generation; quality-focused.

title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
summary: TextGrad backpropagates natural-language feedback from LLMs through a computation graph to improve components of a compound AI system, with a PyTorch-like API. Demonstrated on QA, code, prompt optimization, molecule design and treatment planning, e.g. raising GPT-4o zero-shot GPQA from 51% to 55%.
key_idea: Automatic 'differentiation' via textual feedback for optimizing variables in compound AI graphs.
relevance_rationale: Widely used generic optimizer for compound systems; quality-focused, no cost objective.

title: The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems
summary: Position post arguing that state-of-the-art results increasingly come from systems of multiple interacting components rather than single models. Identifies co-optimizing non-differentiable components (e.g., via DSPy) and cost-quality management (e.g., FrugalGPT-style routing) as core open problems.
key_idea: Defines compound AI systems and frames their end-to-end optimization and cost control as a research agenda.
relevance_rationale: Framing document for the C4 cluster; motivates per-component optimization and cost-aware design.
found_via: seed: The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems (BAIR blog)

title: Collaborative Performance Prediction for Large Language Models
summary: Collaborative Performance Prediction treats model-by-task scores like a recommender matrix, using historical results and design factors to predict LLM downstream performance better than scaling laws.
key_idea: Collaborative filtering for LLM performance prediction.
relevance_rationale: Recsys-style prediction of which model will do well.

title: Generative Verifiers: Reward Modeling as Next-Token Prediction
summary: Trains verifiers with next-token prediction jointly on verification and generation, allowing chain-of-thought verification and majority voting over verifications; outperforms discriminative verifiers and LLM-as-a-Judge with 16-64% gains in best-of-N problems solved.
key_idea: Reward modeling as next-token prediction.
relevance_rationale: Verifier design choice with a tunable compute budget.

title: Privacy-preserved LLM Cascade via CoT-enhanced Policy Learning
summary: Proposes a chain-of-thought-enhanced policy for deciding when an on-device LLM should defer to a server LLM, accounting for privacy leakage as well as cost and quality.
key_idea: Privacy-aware deferral policy for local-to-cloud cascades.
relevance_rationale: Cascade deferral with extra enterprise constraint (privacy).

title: xLAM: A Family of Large Action Models to Empower AI Agent Systems
summary: Releases xLAM large action models (1B to 8x22B) trained with a unified pipeline for augmenting and synthesizing agent data, with strong function-calling results.
key_idea: Open family of action models for agents.
relevance_rationale: Candidate small agent backbones.

title: SAUP: Situation Awareness Uncertainty Propagation on LLM Agent
summary: Propagates uncertainty across every step of an agent's decision process with situation-aware weights, improving AUROC by up to 20% over final-step estimates.
key_idea: Aggregate per-step uncertainty over agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Trajectory-level uncertainty for escalation.

title: WildChat: 1M ChatGPT Interaction Logs in the Wild
summary: WildChat is a corpus of 1M opt-in user-ChatGPT conversations (over 2.5M turns) with timestamps and demographic metadata.
key_idea: Real-world ChatGPT interaction logs.
relevance_rationale: Public production-like logs for router training and analysis.

title: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
summary: GPTSwarm represents agents as computational graphs whose nodes query LLMs and whose edges carry information, and optimizes both node prompts and edge connectivity automatically. Edge optimization prunes or adds inter-agent links, making orchestration itself learnable.
key_idea: Treat multi-agent systems as optimizable graphs and learn which edges to keep.
relevance_rationale: Foundation for topology/pruning work (AgentPrune, G-Designer); not cost-driven itself.
found_via: arXiv title search: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs | seed: GPTSwarm

title: Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning and Coding with LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces sample budget by up to 7.9x with average accuracy drop below 0.1% (17 datasets, three LLMs)
summary: Adjusts the number of self-consistency samples per question with a lightweight stopping rule based on agreement so far.
key_idea: Adaptive number of samples per question.
relevance_rationale: Early foundational adaptive sampling method.
found_via: GitHub list: Awesome-Efficient-Reasoning-LLMs (snowball: related work of sui-2025-stop-overthinking) | hf-papers search: self-consistency cost efficient adaptive

title: ReST meets ReAct: Self-Improvement for Multi-Step Reasoning LLM Agent
summary: Iterative ReST-style self-improvement of a search agent with AI-feedback ranking, then distilling into models two orders of magnitude smaller with comparable performance.
key_idea: Self-improve then distill agent into much smaller models.
relevance_rationale: Agent distillation with AI feedback.

title: Prediction-powered inference
summary: Introduces prediction-powered inference, which combines many model predictions with a small labeled set to produce valid confidence intervals for population quantities.
key_idea: Valid inference from predictions plus a small labeled correction set.
relevance_rationale: Foundation for judge-assisted evaluation of routing policies with guarantees.

title: PPI++: Efficient Prediction-Powered Inference
summary: PPI++ makes prediction-powered inference computationally light and adapts automatically to prediction quality, so its intervals always improve on labeled-only ones.
key_idea: Adaptive, efficient prediction-powered inference.
relevance_rationale: Practical estimator for evaluating routing with judge labels.

title: GPTCache: An Open-Source Semantic Cache for LLM Applications Enabling Faster Answers and Cost Savings
cost_reduction_reported: response speed improves 2-10x on cache hits
summary: Describes GPTCache, an open-source library that intercepts LLM calls, embeds the query, and returns a stored response when a semantically similar query is found in a vector store. It supports multiple embedding models, vector stores and similarity evaluators and integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex.
key_idea: Embedding-similarity cache in front of an LLM API to skip repeated or paraphrased calls.
relevance_rationale: Canonical open-source semantic cache; a baseline cost lever at the query level.

title: How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time?
venue_or_source: Special Issue 5: Grappling With the Generative AI Revolution
summary: Compares March and June 2023 versions of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on several tasks and finds large behavior changes, such as GPT-4 prime identification falling from 84% to 51% accuracy. Highlights the need for continuous monitoring of LLM services.
key_idea: The same API model can change substantially over months.
relevance_rationale: Canonical evidence for non-stationarity in the arms a router selects among.

title: Punica: Multi-Tenant LoRA Serving
cost_reduction_reported: 12x higher throughput serving multiple LoRA models vs state-of-the-art systems with 2 ms added latency per token
summary: Multi-tenant LoRA serving with a CUDA kernel that batches operations across different adapters, holding one copy of the base model per GPU.
key_idea: Batch across LoRA adapters sharing one base model.
relevance_rationale: Multi-specialist serving economics.

title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
cost_reduction_reported: time-to-first-token improved 8x on GPU and 60x on CPU for long prompts while maintaining output accuracy
summary: Prompt Cache precomputes and stores attention states for reusable prompt segments (system messages, templates, documents) declared via a markup schema, reusing them whenever they appear in a prompt, not only as an exact prefix, while keeping positions consistent.
key_idea: Modular, position-aware reuse of attention states for recurring prompt segments.
relevance_rationale: Foundational KV reuse beyond exact prefixes; relevant for shared agent context.
found_via: Prompt Cache modular attention reuse low-latency inference

title: Fine-Tuning Llama-2: A Comprehensive Case Study for Tailoring Models to Unique Applications
cost_reduction_reported: Fine-tuned Llama-2-13B reaches 98% on ViGGO functional representation and fine-tuned 7B/13B about 90% on SQL generation, outperforming GPT-4; on GSM8K fine-tuned 13B improves 28% to 47% but stays behind GPT-4
summary: Practitioner case study fine-tuning Llama-2 on three tasks: structured-output tasks (functional representation, SQL) see small fine-tuned models beat GPT-4, while math reasoning improves but remains behind GPT-4.
key_idea: Specialization wins on structured tasks, less on open reasoning.
relevance_rationale: Practical guide to where small fine-tuned models can replace frontier calls.
found_via: known-item fetch: Anyscale blog fine-tuning Llama-2

title: Tryage: Real-time, intelligent Routing of User Prompts to Large Language Models
summary: Tryage uses a language-model 'perceptive router' to predict downstream performance of expert models from a library on each prompt, then combines these predictions with user-specified constraints such as model size or recency. Users can move along a Pareto front between accuracy and secondary objectives.
key_idea: Predict per-expert performance on a prompt and optimize a constraint-aware objective over a model library.
relevance_rationale: Early model-library router; less relevant to frontier API cost but introduces the Pareto framing.

title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
cost_reduction_reported: Fine-tuned 770M T5 outperforms few-shot 540B PaLM using only 80% of available data on a benchmark
summary: Extracts rationales from an LLM and trains small task-specific models with multi-task label and rationale prediction, beating LLMs with much less training data.
key_idea: Use teacher rationales as extra supervision for small task models.
relevance_rationale: Canonical specialization-by-distillation result.

title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: up to 20x prompt compression with little performance loss on GSM8K/BBH/ShareGPT/Arxiv-March23
summary: Coarse-to-fine prompt compression that uses a small language model to drop low-information tokens. A budget controller allocates compression across prompt parts (instructions, demonstrations, question), and an iterative token-level algorithm models dependencies between kept tokens; the small model is instruction-tuned to align with the target LLM.
key_idea: Use a small LM's perplexity to prune prompt tokens before sending to an expensive black-box LLM.
relevance_rationale: Core prompt-compression technique that directly cuts input-token cost for API-served agents.

title: LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression
cost_reduction_reported: up to 17.1% accuracy gain over the original prompt with ~4x fewer tokens on NaturalQuestions (GPT-3.5-Turbo); cost savings of $28.5 and $27.4 per 1,000 samples on LongBench and ZeroScrolls
summary: Extends LLMLingua to long-context settings by making compression question-aware, reordering documents to counter position bias, and allocating dynamic compression ratios across documents. It shows compression can both cut cost and improve accuracy in long-context RAG.
key_idea: Question-aware compression plus reordering fixes both cost and lost-in-the-middle effects.
relevance_rationale: Long-context compression directly applicable to RAG-heavy and tool-output-heavy agent steps.

title: When Does Confidence-Based Cascade Deferral Suffice?
summary: Characterises the optimal cascade deferral rule and shows when simple confidence-based deferral fails: specialist downstream models, label noise and distribution shift. Post-hoc learned deferral fixes these cases.
key_idea: Theory of when confidence thresholds suffice for cascades.
relevance_rationale: Foundational theory used by LLM cascade papers.

title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
summary: Introduces semantic entropy, which clusters sampled answers by meaning before computing entropy, making uncertainty more predictive of QA accuracy.
key_idea: Semantic entropy over meaning clusters.
relevance_rationale: Signal behind semantic-agreement cascades.
found_via: snowball: related work of cascade papers (verified on arXiv) | seed

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
cost_reduction_reported: 2-4x throughput at the same latency vs FasterTransformer and Orca
summary: PagedAttention stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks managed like OS virtual memory pages, nearly eliminating fragmentation and enabling KV sharing within and across requests; vLLM builds a high-throughput serving engine on it.
key_idea: Page the KV cache to eliminate memory waste and enable sharing.
relevance_rationale: De facto open serving substrate; the baseline for nearly all agent-serving work.

title: OrchestraLLM: Efficient Orchestration of Language Models for Dialogue State Tracking
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces computational costs by over 50% while improving performance vs LLM only (abstract)
summary: OrchestraLLM routes dialogue state tracking instances between a small and large LM by retrieving nearest exemplars from pools where each model was reliable and taking a majority vote.
key_idea: Exemplar-retrieval SLM/LLM routing.
relevance_rationale: Simple kNN routing in a structured task.

title: Compressing Context to Enhance Inference Efficiency of Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: 50% reduction in context cost, 36% lower inference memory and 32% lower inference time, with a 0.023 BERTScore and 0.038 faithfulness drop
summary: Selective Context prunes lexical units (tokens, phrases, sentences) with low self-information computed by a small causal LM. It is one of the earliest filtering-style prompt compression baselines.
key_idea: Drop low self-information spans from the context.
relevance_rationale: Baseline training-free compression technique that later agent-context methods compare against.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
summary: Compares outcome and process supervision for training reward models on math reasoning and finds process-supervised reward models are markedly better at selecting correct solutions. Releases PRM800K step-level human labels and shows active learning improves label efficiency.
key_idea: Step-level (process) reward models beat outcome reward models for verification.
relevance_rationale: Canonical PRM paper; the basis for step-level quality signals in agent trajectories.

title: Generating with Confidence: Uncertainty Quantification for Black-box Large Language Models
summary: Studies black-box uncertainty and confidence metrics for NLG based on dispersion among sampled responses, applied to selective generation where low-confidence outputs are rejected or sent for further assessment.
key_idea: Black-box UQ for selective generation.
relevance_rationale: Directly applicable to escalation with API-only models.

title: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
summary: DyLAN picks a team of agents for a task via an unsupervised Agent Importance Score computed on a preliminary trial, then lets the selected agents collaborate over a dynamic communication structure. It reports better results than fixed-team baselines at moderate compute and up to 25% accuracy gains on some MMLU subjects from team selection alone.
key_idea: Select which agents participate using contribution scores from a trial run.
relevance_rationale: Agent-selection and pruning precursor to AgentPrune/AgentDropout; cost is secondary.

title: (Why) Is My Prompt Getting Worse? Rethinking Regression Testing for Evolving LLM APIs
venue_or_source: 2024 IEEE/ACM 3rd International Conference on AI Engineering – Software Engineering for AI (CAIN)
summary: Case study showing that silent updates and deprecations of LLM APIs cause regressions in downstream prompts (toxicity detection). Argues that regression testing for LLM APIs needs new approaches because of fuzzy correctness, prompt brittleness and non-determinism.
key_idea: LLM API updates silently regress downstream behavior, requiring dedicated regression testing.
relevance_rationale: Model-swap drift is a core risk for any learned router or config; motivates continuous re-evaluation.

title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
summary: Detects hallucinations in black-box LLMs by sampling multiple responses and checking consistency of facts, needing no external database or logits.
key_idea: Inconsistency across samples flags hallucination.
relevance_rationale: Widely used zero-resource hallucination signal.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
summary: MemGPT applies OS-style virtual memory to LLMs: the model moves information between a small in-context working set and external storage via function calls, giving the illusion of unbounded context for long documents and multi-session conversations.
key_idea: Virtual context management: page information in and out of the context window.
relevance_rationale: Foundational memory architecture for keeping agent contexts small.

title: Leveraging Implicit Feedback from Deployment Data in Dialogue
summary: Uses publicly released BlenderBot deployment conversations to learn from implicit signals such as the length, sentiment and reactions of the following user turn. Human evaluation shows improvements, but some proxies such as conversation length push the model toward controversial outputs.
key_idea: Next-user-turn signals from deployment logs act as implicit quality labels, with proxy-hacking risks.
relevance_rationale: Early production-data study of implicit feedback proxies and their failure modes.

title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
cost_reduction_reported: Fine-tuned LLaMA surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls
summary: Fine-tunes LLaMA on API documentation-derived instructions with retriever-aware training to produce accurate API calls and reduce hallucinated usage, surpassing GPT-4 on APIBench.
key_idea: Specialized small model for API calls.
relevance_rationale: Early specialization beating a frontier model.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
summary: Constructs ToolBench from 16,464 RapidAPI APIs with ChatGPT-generated instructions and solution paths (via depth-first search decision trees), fine-tuning LLaMA into ToolLLaMA with an API retriever.
key_idea: Large synthetic tool-use data enables open tool agents.
relevance_rationale: Canonical tool-use distillation.

title: Self-Evaluation Improves Selective Generation in Large Language Models
summary: Turns open-ended generation into token-level self-evaluation (multi-way or point-wise, with a none-of-the-above option) to get better-calibrated scores for selective generation.
key_idea: Self-evaluation scores beat sequence likelihood for abstention.
relevance_rationale: Signal usable for deciding when to escalate.
found_via: arXiv title search: selective generation large language models | keyword: confidence estimation

title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters
signals_used: unified paging of adapters and KV
cost_reduction_reported: up to 4x throughput vs HuggingFace PEFT and vLLM with naive LoRA support, serving orders of magnitude more adapters
summary: Serves thousands of LoRA adapters on shared base weights with unified paging for adapter weights and KV caches plus custom kernels for heterogeneous batching.
key_idea: Serve many fine-tuned specialists cheaply on one base model.
relevance_rationale: Makes per-task specialized small models economical to serve.

title: When is Off-Policy Evaluation (Reward Modeling) Useful in Contextual Bandits? A Data-Centric Perspective
summary: Proposes DataCOPE, a data-centric framework that forecasts how accurate off-policy evaluation will be on a given logged dataset, identifies subgroups where OPE is unreliable, and compares data-collection strategies.
key_idea: Assess whether a logged dataset can support OPE for a target policy before trusting it.
relevance_rationale: Diagnoses when router or config logs are adequate for OPE.
found_via: query: abs:"off-policy evaluation" AND abs:"large language model"

title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
summary: For RLHF models, verbalised confidence is often better calibrated than token probabilities, cutting expected calibration error by about 50% relative.
key_idea: Verbalised confidence can be the better escalation signal for RLHF models.
relevance_rationale: Signal choice for black-box cascades.
found_via: snowball: related work of cascade papers (verified on arXiv) | keyword: verbalized confidence

title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
summary: Builds a process reward model trained from automatically constructed step labels (via rollouts estimating whether a step leads to the correct answer), avoiding human annotation. Used both for reranking and step-wise PPO; e.g., Mistral-7B rises from 77.9% to 84.1% on GSM8K with PPO and to 89.1% with verification.
key_idea: Automatic step labels from completion rollouts train a PRM.
relevance_rationale: Shows PRMs can be built cheaply without human labels, relevant to agent PRMs.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
summary: Benchmarks black-box confidence elicitation (prompting, sampling, aggregation) for calibration and failure prediction; finds verbal overconfidence and that consistency across samples helps.
key_idea: Black-box confidence elicitation benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Background for choosing escalation signals.
found_via: snowball: related work of cascade papers (verified on arXiv) | keyword: confidence estimation

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
cost_reduction_reported: compression rate as low as 6% with minimal loss in performance on language modeling and open-domain QA
summary: Trains extractive and abstractive compressors that turn retrieved documents into short summaries before they are placed in context; the compressor can output nothing when retrieval is unhelpful. This lowers RAG inference cost while often keeping accuracy.
key_idea: Compress retrieved documents into query-focused summaries, or skip them entirely.
relevance_rationale: Transferable to compressing tool/retrieval outputs inside agent loops.
found_via: RECOMP compressing retrieved documents selective augmentation

title: How Predictable Are Large Language Model Capabilities? A Case Study on BIG-bench
signals_used: experiment records: model family, size, task, shots
summary: Trains an MLP on BIG-bench experiment records to predict LLM performance on new configurations (R^2 > 95% on random splits) and searches for a small informative task subset.
key_idea: Performance prediction from past experiment records.
relevance_rationale: Predicting configuration performance from logs of past runs.

title: Agent Lumos: Unified and Modular Training for Open-Source Language Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Lumos surpasses GPT-4/3.5-based agents on complex QA and web tasks
summary: Trains modular open-source agents (planning, grounding, execution modules) on unified annotations converted from existing benchmarks with GPT-4.
key_idea: Modular small agents trained on unified data.
relevance_rationale: Module-level specialization.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: AgentLM-70B comparable to GPT-3.5-turbo on unseen agent tasks
summary: Builds AgentInstruct, a dataset of filtered GPT-4 interaction trajectories, and mixes it with general instructions to tune Llama 2 into AgentLM, preserving general ability while improving agent skills.
key_idea: Hybrid agent-trajectory plus general instruction tuning.
relevance_rationale: Classic trajectory-SFT recipe.

title: LMSYS-Chat-1M: A Large-Scale Real-World LLM Conversation Dataset
summary: Releases one million real conversations with 25 LLMs collected from the Vicuna demo and Chatbot Arena, with use cases such as moderation models and benchmark building.
key_idea: Large real-world LLM conversation log dataset.
relevance_rationale: Public proxy for production traffic to train/evaluate routers.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
summary: Shows strong LLM judges (GPT-4) agree with human preferences over 80% of the time, similar to human-human agreement, using MT-Bench and early Chatbot Arena data; releases votes and conversations.
key_idea: LLM-as-a-judge validated against crowdsourced preferences.
relevance_rationale: Judge signal and Arena data underpin router training and online evaluation.
found_via: OpenAlex title: Chatbot Arena | keyword: LLM-as-a-judge

title: JudgeLM: Fine-tuned Large Language Models are Scalable Judges
summary: Fine-tunes LLMs (7B-33B) on GPT-4 judgments to create scalable judges, addressing position, knowledge and format biases with swap augmentation and reference support/drop.
